articles.title: Israel’s intent is to prevent Palestinians from existing as a group: Justice Muralidhar
articles.summary: Israel implements policies to maximize the occupation of Palestinian territories and minimize the Palestinian population, according to Justice Srinivasan Muralidhar. Speaking on a podcast, the chair of the UN-appointed Independent International Commission of Inquiry stated the commission demonstrated Israel's intent to prevent Palestinians from existing as a group while gathering evidence of war crimes in occupied territories.
articles.description: In a strong indictment of Israel’s policies in the occupied Palestinian territories, Justice Srinivasan Muralidhar, chair of the UN-appointed Independent International Commission of Inquiry, has accused Israel of seeking to expand its occupation while reducing the Palestinian population

articles.headline: Iran military warns third conflict with US and Israel will be costly
articles.title: How would Tehran respond if the US and Israel bomb Iran again?
articles.summary: Iran military officials warned that a renewed war with the United States and Israel would be longer and more costly than expected, utilizing new weapons and asymmetric warfare. Former Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps commander Hossein Kanani Moghaddam said Iranian forces are in better operational shape, while analysts noted ongoing domestic security concerns and intelligence weaknesses within the regime.
articles.description: Iran has retained significant offensive capability, but civilians and critical infrastructure remain largely exposed.

articles.headline: Iran says US talks could resume ‘within a short period’ if demands are met
articles.title: Iran says US talks could resume ‘within a short period’ if demands are met

articles.headline: India manufacturing sector activity growth eases in October amid softer output and new orders
articles.title: Manufacturing PMI eases to 54.7 in October, but overseas demand at six-month high
articles.summary: India's manufacturing sector growth slowed in October as output and new orders increased at milder rates, according to the HSBC India Manufacturing Purchasing Managers' Index compiled by S&P Global. The seasonally adjusted index fell to 54.7 from 55.1 in September. HSBC Chief India Economist Pranjul Bhandari noted that strong international demand pushed new export orders to a six-month high while input cost inflation retreated to its lowest level since February.
articles.description: Even as demand increased, the survey respondents said that cost pressures eased in October

articles.headline: China urges political solutions to resolve conflict in West Asia
articles.title: West Asia conflict: China's Foreign Minister pushes for dialogue
articles.summary: Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi stated on November 2, 2026, that all parties in the West Asia conflict should prioritize political solutions rather than armed conflict. Speaking in Beijing with Ali Bagheri Kani of Iran, Mr. Wang emphasized negotiation. Additionally, Chinese President Xi Jinping told Omani leader Sultan Haitham bin Tariq al-Said that the region should not become a battleground for great-power rivalry.
articles.description: Dialogue ‌and negotiation are the way ‌to ⁠resolve West Asia conflicts, Chinese FM ⁠told Ali Bagheri Kani, the Deputy Secretary of the Iran Supreme National Security Council

articles.headline: Iran considers two-day plan to reopen Strait of Hormuz
articles.title: Iran says considering two-day plan to reopen Hormuz
articles.summary: Iran announced on November 2, 2026, that it is evaluating a two-day plan to reopen the Strait of Hormuz if the United States accepts specific demands, including ending the West Asia war, lifting oil sanctions, and unfreezing assets. Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baqaei stated that messages are being exchanged via mediators, while U.S. and Israeli officials continue to issue military threats.
articles.description: “The possibility of implementing this plan in two days is another indication of Iran's good-faith approach,” Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baqaei said

articles.headline: Sudan files formal complaints against Ethiopia over drone attacks
articles.title: Sudan files complaints against Ethiopia with UN over deadly drone spree
articles.summary: Sudan lodged complaints with the United Nations Security Council and the African Union regarding deadly drone attacks originating from Ethiopian territory. The Sudanese Ministry of Foreign Affairs accused the Rapid Support Forces of using Ethiopian bases to target civilian sites. A report from the Transitional Sovereignty Council stated that 70 assaults since February 2026 resulted in hundreds of casualties.
articles.description: One-way drone attacks have killed or wounded 484 civilians since February, Khartoum says.

articles.headline: Displaced Sudanese families struggle amid worsening food shortages and famine
articles.title: As aid situation worsens, displaced Sudanese worry about warnings of famine
articles.summary: Displaced Sudanese citizens across camps face severe food insecurity and declining humanitarian aid as the conflict between the Sudanese Armed Forces and Rapid Support Forces continues. Aisha Adam, who fled to Port Sudan, works daily to buy basic supplies. Meanwhile, the World Food Programme and the United States Department of State warned of a rising famine risk affecting millions nationwide.
articles.description: Sudan's displaced people now face a mounting food crisis, with warnings of famine.

articles.headline: Scientists react as artificial intelligence disrupts foundational computer science hypotheses
articles.title: Shock and regret: scientists react to AI roiling life’s work
articles.summary: OpenAI and Anthropic announced that artificial intelligence models disproved the exponential time hypothesis, which posits that certain computational problems require exhaustive answers. Originators Russell Impagliazzo, Ramamohan Paturi, and researcher Ryan Williams are organizing an independent review. The developments have sparked academic debate regarding the future of human research, tool accessibility, and the rapid pace of technological change.
articles.description: OpenAI and Anthropic each said last week that one of their AI models had disproved the exponential time hypothesis

articles.title: Trump makes controversial claims at final Republican campaign rallies
articles.description: Donald Trump made a series of provocative remarks during his final Republican campaign rallies.

articles.headline: European authorities inspect seven passenger flights following anonymous bomb threats
articles.title: Seven flights across Europe targeted by suspected bomb threats
articles.summary: Authorities across Europe inspected seven passenger planes after receiving anonymous bomb threats, including flights operated by Ryanair and Scandinavian Airlines. The UK government dismissed the incidents as malicious hoaxes. Bulgarian and Spanish officials confirmed no explosives were found following standard security protocols, while aviation experts noted the unusual nature of the coordinated threats.
articles.description: Planes in Poland, Spain, Bulgaria and Italy have been checked for explosives following separate threats.

articles.headline: North coastal Andhra Pradesh records early rainfall from approaching Cyclone Murasu
articles.title: Rain begins in north Andhra ahead of Cyclone Murasu
articles.summary: North coastal Andhra Pradesh received initial rainfall on Monday from severe cyclonic storm Murasu moving from the Bay of Bengal. Kakinada Rural mandal recorded 51.75 mm of rain between 8.30 a.m. and noon, according to data from the Andhra Pradesh Directorate of Economics and Statistics. The India Meteorological Department expects landfall between Monday night and Tuesday morning near Ongole, with officials warning the damage depends on storm strength.
articles.description: Kakinada (Rural) mandal records 51.75 mm by noon; the storm is likely to cross the coast near Ongole tonight

articles.headline: Why ISRO’s latest success matters more than it appears | The Hindu Editorial
articles.title: Why ISRO’s latest success matters more than it appears | The Hindu Editorial

articles.headline: India evacuates thousands as Cyclone Murasu approaches Andhra Pradesh
articles.title: Thousands evacuated as India braces for second cyclone in a week
articles.summary: Authorities in Andhra Pradesh began moving residents from low-lying coastal areas as Cyclone Murasu approached the region on November 2, 2026. Prakhar Jain of the Andhra Pradesh State Disaster Management Authority stated that about 2,000 individuals had been relocated by Monday, with plans to reach 30,000. The India Meteorological Department projected wind speeds of up to 110 kilometres per hour, threatening power supplies and infrastructure across multiple districts.
articles.description: Cyclone Murasu expected to hit near Ongole late Monday with wind speeds of 100-110km/h, Meteorological Department says.

articles.headline: Apple integrates Siri AI with third-party applications in iOS update
articles.title: Apple starts giving Siri AI access to third-party apps
articles.summary: Apple released the iOS twenty-seven point three developer preview on Tuesday, allowing developers to integrate Siri AI features across third-party applications. The update enables the voice assistant to process natural language prompts and use personal context to complete multi-step tasks. Expanded capabilities are also being introduced to numerous native Apple applications including Calendar, Mail, and Maps.
articles.description: Apple will now let Siri AI perform actions across third-party apps. As part of the iOS 27.3 update rolling out on Tuesday, Apple announced developers can now integrate Siri AI's new features in "all apps," allowing the voice assistant to draw on a user's personal context, process natural language prompts, and use on-screen awareness to […]

articles.headline: Subroto Bagchi warns Karnataka's tech success leaves non-urban regions behind
articles.title: Staggering white-collar success of Bengaluru has left a non-urban world behind, says Bagchi
articles.summary: Speaking at the Bengaluru Skill Summit on November 4, 2026, Karnataka's Skill Vision Group chairman Subroto Bagchi warned that Bengaluru's IT and biotech success has left non-urban areas behind. To prevent youth unrest, he advocated reforming vocational education and implementing Karnataka's inclusive skill policy to uplift grassroots technical schools and empower rural communities.
articles.description: While the IITs have marched confidently forward since the 1950s, the ITIs have walked backwards. These two paths must operate stereophonically, cooperating in the exact same direction, says newly appointed Chairman of Karnataka’s Skill Vision Group

articles.headline: United Nations demands independent investigation into human rights worker's death in Houthi custody
articles.title: UN staffer’s death in custody exposes Houthi ‘political extortion’ in Yemen
articles.summary: The United Nations is demanding a transparent investigation into the death of Mohammad el-Shami, a human rights employee who died in Houthi detention in Yemen. UN High Commissioner for Human Rights Volker Turk urged authorities in Sanaa to disclose medical records and preserve evidence. El-Shami was arbitrarily detained in June 2024 among dozens of targeted personnel, making him the second UN staff member to die in custody.
articles.description: Following a UN staffer's death, rights experts expose systematic abuses and demand international accountability in Yemen

articles.headline: Binance customers withdraw billions in assets following major cryptocurrency hack
articles.title: Binance users withdraw $3.6bn after largest-ever crypto hack
articles.summary: Binance users withdrew 3.6 billion dollars on November 1, 2026, as the cryptocurrency exchange reopened following a massive cyberattack impacting 6.3 billion dollars in digital assets. The Federal Bureau of Investigation and other organisations attributed the breach to North Korea. Binance stated that it has covered approximately 95 percent of the stolen funds using corporate reserves and insurance funds.
articles.description: The exchange froze transactions following the incident which has been linked to a North Korean group.

articles.headline: The unending purge in Xi’s China
articles.title: The unending purge in Xi’s China
articles.description: China’s Fifth Plenum confirmed the expulsion of 33 Central Committee members, including 16 Generals, signalling that Xi Jinping’s anti-corruption purge is far from over; the purge has raised questions about PLA leadership and combat readiness, while Xi’s succession plans remain unclear ahead of the 2027 Party Congress

articles.title: Hormuz shipping still faces major risks
articles.description: The Strait of Hormuz remains dangerous and costly for shipping, despite US claims that it is open.

articles.headline: Kochi Corporation approves thirty projects worth fifteen hundred crore rupees
articles.title: Kochi Corporation clears 30 projects worth ₹1,500 crore for Urban Challenge Fund
articles.summary: The Kochi Corporation Council approved a concept note on November 3, 2026, featuring thirty infrastructure and welfare projects worth over fifteen hundred crore rupees for funding under the Urban Challenge Fund. Mayor V.K. Minimol stated the initiative prioritises revenue-generating schemes, while councillors debated balancing commercial developments with existing welfare and community commitments.
articles.description: Projects include mobility hubs, civic tower, cultural district and waste-processing facility under Kochi@2050 vision; Union government to provide 25% of project cost as grant; Opposition councillors raise concerns over prioritising revenue-generating projects and use of land earmarked for welfare initiatives

articles.headline: Telugu Desam Party wins Pulivendula municipal chairperson seat after decades
articles.title: Local body polls in Andhra: TDP breaches YSRCP’s fortress of Pulivendula after four decades
articles.summary: Telugu Desam Party candidate T. Geetha Kumari won the Pulivendula municipal chairperson seat on November 3, 2026, defeating YSRCP opponent Y.S. Prameelamma by 13,875 votes. This victory ended a four-decade political monopoly by the YS family. Meanwhile, courts dismissed opposition requests for repolling, and code of conduct violation cases were filed against 72 YSRCP leaders.
articles.description: TDP’s Geetha Kumari wins Pulivendula municipal chairperson seat by defeating YSRCP president Y.S. Jagan Mohan Redddy’s aunt Prameelamma with a majority of 13,875 votes

articles.headline: Andhra Pradesh mandates 360-hour semester internships for undergraduate students
articles.title: Andhra Pradesh makes 360-hour semester internships mandatory for UG students
articles.summary: The Andhra Pradesh State Council of Higher Education announced a mandatory 360-hour semester internship for undergraduate students, beginning November 16, 2026. APSCHE Chairman S. Vijaya Bhaskar Rao stated the initiative aims to boost graduate employability through structured industry linkages. Students must register via the Institute-Industry Connect portal to secure verified placements.
articles.description: Internships to be incorporated into the final-year curriculum of three-year and four-year UG programmes; priority to stipend-based internships available through the Institute-Industry Connect portal

articles.headline: Michigan voters cast ballots in high-stakes United States Senate race
articles.title: Michigan US Senate race: Rogers, El-Sayed urge turnout for critical race
articles.summary: Voters in Michigan are participating in a closely watched United States Senate election between Democrat Abdul El-Sayed and Republican Mike Rogers to replace retiring Senator Gary Peters. The competitive race could determine chamber control and features heavy national scrutiny, historic Department of Justice monitoring, and debates over progressive policies and foreign aid.
articles.description: Abdul El-Sayed hopes to become the first Muslim US senator as Michigan's Senate race reaches its critical final hours.

articles.headline: National Conference leader Aga Syed Ruhullah resigns from party and Lok Sabha seat
articles.title: ‘I set myself free from NC, this is my azaadi,’ says resigned leader Aga Syed Ruhullah
articles.summary: Aga Syed Ruhullah resigned from the ruling National Conference and the Srinagar Lok Sabha seat on Tuesday, accusing top leaders Dr. Farooq Abdullah and Omar Abdullah of betraying public promises and electoral exploitation. The 48-year-old Shia cleric criticized the 2019 abrogation of Article 370 and hinted at launching a new political campaign across Jammu and Kashmir.
articles.description: He accused Dr. Farooq Abdullah and Omar Abdullah of ‘betraying promises made to the people and misusing him for electoral gains’

articles.headline: Tamil Nadu launches battery energy storage systems policy to boost grid stability
articles.title: Tamil Nadu government releases three-year BESS policy
articles.summary: The Tamil Nadu government published a three-year storage policy on November 4, 2026, aiming to deploy 2.5 gigawatts of battery capacity. The Tamil Nadu Power Distribution Corporation will procure this capacity in the first phase. The framework mandates installations for new solar projects starting April 1, 2027, and offers transmission charge waivers to support the state's twenty-nine gigawatts of renewable energy.
articles.description: The policy aims to deploy 2.5 GW/10 GWh of Battery Energy Storage System during this period. The TNPDC will procure BESS capacity aggregating to 2,500 MW/10,000 MWh from eligible BESS projects

articles.headline: Palestinian Americans turn to US flags to protect West Bank homes
articles.title: Palestinian Americans turn to US flags to protect West Bank homes
articles.description: Palestinian Americans in the occupied West Bank are putting up US flags, to fend off pogroms by Israeli settlers.

articles.headline: King Charles expresses profound personal sorrow over transatlantic slave trade
articles.title: UK’s King Charles expresses ‘sorrow’ in Antigua over slave trade
articles.summary: King Charles III stated at the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting in Antigua and Barbuda on Tuesday that the transatlantic slave trade fills him with profound personal sorrow. While leaders including Guyanese President Mohamed Irfaan Ali called for a formal apology, the British monarch stopped short of issuing one, focusing instead on improving education and addressing climate resilience.
articles.description: Caribbean nations call for reparations as King Charles stops short of issuing an apology for colonial-era slavery.

articles.headline: Assam government seeks CBI probe into floods and bans polygamy for employees
articles.title: Assam to seek CBI probe to find flood cause; sack government employee if involved in polygamy: CM Himanta
articles.summary: The Assam government decided on November 3, 2026, to request a Central Bureau of Investigation probe into the exact cause of devastating floods in Sivasagar and Charaideo districts. Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma announced that any government employee involved in polygamy will face termination. This rule applies across all religions following the implementation of the Uniform Civil Code in the state.
articles.description: The Assam government has decided to terminate an employee, irrespective of religion, if he is found to be involved in polygamy, Himanta Biswa Sarma said

articles.headline: Indian political consultants deploy shadow social media campaigns to influence foreign elections
articles.title: Shadowy Indian election ‘consultants’ add US midterms to global footprint
articles.summary: Specialised private companies based in India are operating coordinated online influence networks to manipulate international elections, including the United States midterms and Kenya's presidential race. According to researchers, these firms use anonymous accounts, premium virtual private networks, and altered content on platforms like Meta and Google to evade regulatory standards and avoid public scrutiny.
articles.description: India's election consultants are exporting covert campaign tactics to manipulate elections worldwide, including the US.

articles.headline: Israeli forces withdraw from Hebron after ten-day military siege
articles.title: Hebron governor says Israeli forces withdraw from city after 10-day siege
articles.summary: Palestinian security forces have assumed control of Hebron following the departure of Israeli troops who concluded a ten-day military operation. Governor Khaled Dudin confirmed that displaced residents could return home. The siege, initiated after an October 23 shooting attack that killed two Israeli soldiers, resulted in significant property destruction, infrastructure damage, and the displacement of more than 3,300 people.
articles.description: Hebron Mayor Youssef al-Jaabari says families forced from their homes can return and students can go to school.

articles.headline: Protesters clash with security forces in Manipur following recovery of bodies
articles.title: Agitators clash with security forces in Manipur's Kangpokpi after recovery of missing youths' bodies
articles.summary: Demonstrators clashed with security personnel in the Kangpokpi district of Manipur on November 2, 2026, after the mutilated remains of two missing youths were discovered in Senapati. Law enforcement deployed tear gas and baton-charged the crowd to disperse stone-throwing agitators. Local officials and community leaders strongly condemned the violence while demanding an independent and transparent investigation into the killings.
articles.description: Protests erupted in several parts of Kangpokpi district on November 1, as agitators burned tyres on many roads and blocked several stretches with logs of wood and boulders

articles.headline: Karnataka High Court initiates contempt proceedings after advocates disrupt court proceedings
articles.title: Karnataka High Court initiates contempt proceedings over ruckus created by lawyers’ group inside Chief Justice’s court hall
articles.summary: The High Court of Karnataka initiated suo motu contempt proceedings on November 3, 2026, against unidentified advocates who barged into the Chief Justice and other court halls to disrupt proceedings. A Division Bench issued notice to the Advocates’ Association, Bengaluru, after protesters compelled lawyers to leave. Meanwhile, an association delegation met Home Minister Priyank Kharge to demand enhanced security measures.
articles.description: The High Court of Karnataka on Tuesday began suo motu contempt proceedings against unidentified individuals amongst a group of advocates, who barged into the Chief Justice’s court hall and disrupted proceedings by creating ruckus

articles.headline: Delhi Police suspends ACP Manasvi Vashishta for leading headquarters protest
articles.title: ACP Manasvi Vashishta suspended day after protest outside Delhi police headquarters; lawyer moves HC over ‘police remarks’
articles.summary: Assistant Commissioner of Police Manasvi Vashishta was suspended by Delhi Police sources on November 3, 2026, for violating discipline after joining a protest. On November 2, 2026, roughly 100 personnel gathered outside the Delhi Police headquarters to demand a meeting with Police Commissioner Anurag Kumar following an altercation between officers and lawyers at the Shahdara police station.
articles.description: Manasvi Vashishta had joined around 100 police personnel protesting outside police headquarters against his transfer and that of Shahdara SHO Arun Kumar, after lawyers alleged the two officers had threatened advocates seeking action in an assault case.

articles.headline: IISc Bangalore and several IITs slip in QS Asia University Rankings 2027
articles.title: QS Asia Rankings 2027: IISc Bangalore slips 15 places to 79th
articles.summary: The Indian Institute of Science Bangalore slipped 15 places to 79th in the QS World University Rankings: Asia 2027, released on November 3, 2026. IIT Delhi remained the highest-ranked Indian institution at 66th despite dropping seven spots. While Indian universities faced declines in academic and employer reputations, 27 institutions secured positions in Asia’s top 50 for papers per faculty.

articles.headline: Karnataka High Court orders suo motu PIL over rising violence against advocates
articles.title: Karnataka High Court initiates suo motu PIL on violence against advocates
articles.summary: The High Court of Karnataka initiated a suo motu public interest litigation petition on November 3, 2026, addressing recent violence against lawyers, including murders and attempted assaults. Acting on representations from the Advocates’ Association, Bengaluru, and the Karnataka State Bar Council, the court directed the state government to disclose protective measures and detailed case particulars regarding the attacks.
articles.description: The High Court of Karnataka initiated a suo motu PIL petition on the spate of violence against advocates in the State

articles.headline: Union government plans to simplify visa application forms to boost tourism
articles.title: India set to simplify visa forms
articles.summary: The Indian government plans to simplify visa application forms to meet global standards, with changes expected next year across all 22 categories. Officials stated that redundant and repetitive fields will be reduced by approximately 70% to support the travel and tourism industry. Foreign tourist arrivals reached 91.5 lakh in 2025, remaining below the 2019 pre-pandemic total of 1.093 crore.
articles.description: Redundant fields in the bulky forms will be done away with and the changes are likely to be implemented from next year, says official

articles.headline: Election day vote counting schedule and poll closing times across United States
articles.title: U.S. Midterm Election night agenda: When polls close and when to expect results
articles.summary: Voters across the United States decided thousands of races on November 3, 2026, with polls closing at staggered times from early morning until midnight across different states. The Associated Press and state officials tracked vote counting progress, noting that some states complete tallies quickly on election night while others take several days due to mail-in ballots.
articles.description: With voters deciding thousands of races across the country, keeping track of which races to watch throughout the night and when to expect results can get tricky

articles.headline: Southern India grows wetter as climate zones shift over seven decades
articles.title: Southern India has grown wetter over seven decades, finds IMD study
articles.summary: Southern India has experienced a significant increase in rainfall over the past seven decades, according to a study by scientists from the India Meteorological Department and the Indian Institute of Tropical Meteorology. Researchers found that hot semi-arid regions nearly halved from 1951 to 2020, transitioning into tropical savannah climate zones, which could impact long-term agricultural and water planning across the peninsula.
articles.description: The peninsula’s hot semi-arid zone has nearly halved, with much of it turning into a tropical savannah climate, while north-west India has become drier and hotter

articles.headline: Greenland parliament approves security and resource agreement with United States and Denmark
articles.title: Greenland parliament approves security deal with US, Denmark
articles.summary: Lawmakers in the self-governing Danish territory of Greenland unanimously approved a trilateral security agreement with the United States and Denmark on November 3, 2026. The deal, previously signed in September by US President Donald Trump, Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen and Greenlandic Prime Minister Jens-Frederik Nielsen, aims to bolster Arctic security and allows for the expansion of US military activities.
articles.description: Lawmakers vote 16-0 for trilateral agreement signed in September, while seven abstained.

articles.headline: French students blockade schools and universities demanding education reforms
articles.title: Students blockade dozens of French schools and universities
articles.summary: Students across France blockaded dozens of high schools and universities on November 3, 2026, to protest against education policies and demand increased funding. Authorities reported disruptions at numerous institutions amidst tight security and nationwide protests, while Education Minister Edouard Geffray condemned the actions for depriving students of their fundamental right to an education.
articles.description: After returning from a two-week autumn break, some students resumed their protest campaign on November 2

articles.headline: 'I couldn't be silent': Iranian teen's mother seeking justice after daughter shot dead
articles.title: 'I couldn't be silent': Iranian teen's mother seeking justice after daughter shot dead
articles.description: BBC Panorama follows grieving Samira who - after the killing of Sevda - faces up to the Tehran regime.

articles.headline: Welfare payments will use voter identity cards instead of Aadhaar according to minister
articles.title: Welfare payments will be based on voter IDs, not Aadhaar, says Panchayati Raj Minister
articles.summary: Union Minister for Panchayati Raj Rajiv Ranjan Singh stated on November 3, 2026, that welfare scheme payments will rely on voter identity cards and biometric authentication rather than Aadhaar. Speaking in Gangtok, the minister argued that the proposed shift would eliminate fraudulent entries and ensure benefits reach eligible recipients by improving the overall verification process.
articles.description: At present, welfare payments are linked to Aadhaar; Panchayati Raj Minister says people should now give EPIC number with biometrics

articles.headline: Mother fights Iranian regime after security forces kill teenage daughter
articles.title: Iran killed her teenage daughter - now she is facing up to the regime
articles.summary: Samira fled Iran on foot and went into hiding abroad after her sixteen-year-old daughter Sevda was shot dead by security forces during anti-government protests on January 9, 2026. According to the mother, authorities hindered her search for the body and forced her to blame terrorists for the death. While human rights groups estimate thousands of fatalities, the Iranian embassy claimed protests were hijacked by foreign powers.
articles.description: Samira's 16-year-old daughter Sevda was shot dead as they took part in mass protests in January.

articles.headline: Poland constitutional tribunal president and vice president suspended for one month
articles.title: Poland plunges into crisis over fight for control of constitutional tribunal
articles.summary: Poland's Constitutional Tribunal announced the one-month suspension of its president Bogdan Święczkowski and vice-president Bartłomiej Sochański on October 30, 2026. The order was signed by judge Anna Korwin-Piotrowska amid ongoing legal disputes. Protesters gathered outside the tribunal building while President Karol Nawrocki returned to Warsaw and contested the legitimacy of the judicial body.
articles.description: Ruling bloc led by PM Tusk and Opposition-backed President Nawrocki are at loggerheads over appointments made to the tribunal by each side. Judges to tribunal are appointed by lower house of parliament. Many, including those in ruling camp, call for ‘constitutional reset’ with amendments

articles.headline: South Korea and Turkey strengthen nuclear and defence partnership
articles.title: South Korea, Turkey agree to deepen nuclear energy, defence ties
articles.summary: South Korea and Turkey agreed to expand bilateral ties during a presidential summit on November 3, 2026, in Seoul. Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan and South Korean President Lee Jae Myung discussed cooperation on Turkey Sinop nuclear power plant project and signed financing agreements. articles.description: The two sides agreed that cooperation on Turkey's Sinop nuclear power plant project has been progressing smoothly

articles.headline: North Indian cities record very poor air quality levels
articles.title: Air quality worsens to ‘very poor’ category in Delhi, parts of north India
articles.summary: The overall air quality in Delhi and several north Indian cities deteriorated to the very poor category on November 2, 2026, according to official data. The Central Pollution Control Board reported that Delhi recorded a 24-hour average Air Quality Index of 310 at 8 a.m. The Central government warns that hazardous pollution levels will persist for up to six days, driven by meteorological conditions, vehicle emissions, dust, stubble burning, and post-festive firecrackers.
articles.description: The 24-hour average Air Quality Index (AQI) of Delhi was 310 (very poor) at 8 a.m. on November 2, 2026, as per Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) data

articles.headline: Gunmen kill two police officers protecting polio workers in Pakistan
articles.title: Suspected militants open fire, kill 2 police officers guarding polio workers in Pakistan
articles.summary: Suspected militants on a motorcycle killed two police officers and wounded a third on November 3, 2026, in Pakistan Mohmand district during a door-to-door polio vaccination drive. Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi condemned the attack as intolerable. The incident occurred as Pakistan launched a nationwide campaign to vaccinate 24 million children against the disease, which remains endemic in the country.

articles.headline: South Carolina shrimpers face rising costs and industry challenges ahead of elections

articles.description: Shrimpers worry about fuel costs, tariffs and Trump's proposed cuts to the agency that provides vital weather data.

articles.headline: Saudi coalition intercepts drone as Houthi officials report civilian deaths

articles.summary: The Saudi-led coalition intercepted a drone in the Mecca region on November 3, 2026, while Houthi officials reported that Saudi airstrikes killed 17 people over two days in Yemen. Coalition spokesman Turki al-Malki reported the interception, whereas Houthi military spokesperson Yahya Saree dismissed the allegation as a lie. The United Nations reports that ongoing violence has displaced over 300,000 people recently.
articles.description: Saudi Arabia has accused the Houthis several times of targeting Mecca and Medina, another holy city, accusations the Iran-backed fighters systematically reject

articles.headline: IRDAI sets December 15 deadline for mandatory four-layer motor insurance policy
articles.title: 4-layer motor cover for new private cars, 2-wheelers from Dec. 15: IRDAI
articles.summary: The Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India instructed general insurers to implement a four-layer motor insurance structure for new private cars and two-wheelers starting December 15. The policy integrates mandatory third party and personal accident coverage with optional components for legal liability, occupant personal accidents, and own damage, following directives issued by the Supreme Court to improve transparency.
articles.description: Regulator’s directive follows Supreme Court order mandating a policy structure covering third-party liability, legal liability to occupants, personal accident and own damage

articles.headline: Adani airports CEO tells foreign airlines to shift operations or stop flying
articles.title: Shift to Navi Mumbai or stop flying to Mumbai: Adani Airports CEO tells foreign airlines
articles.summary: Arun Bansal, chief executive officer of Adani Airport Holdings, stated on November 3, 2026, that international airlines unwilling to relocate to Navi Mumbai International Airport could stop flying to Mumbai. The dispute arises as Mumbai International Airport Limited prepares terminal redevelopment work, prompting carrier resistance over split operations, lack of consultation, and passenger impacts during the transition process.
articles.description: Adani Airports Holdings CEO Arun Bansal says, “Like a landlord tells its airlines to vacate his property… we have told airlines you have to vacate from April. After that where you go is your choice.”

articles.headline: Hundreds mourn late Irish Olympian Ciara Mageean at funeral
articles.title: Irish Olympian Ciara Mageean was a 'talented and inspirational human being'
articles.summary: Hundreds of mourners gathered in Portaferry on Tuesday to attend the funeral of former European champion and two-time Olympian Ciara Mageean. The athlete passed away on Sunday following a stage four bowel cancer diagnosis, just weeks after marrying her partner Thomas Moran. Dignitaries, family members, and sports figures paid tribute to her remarkable athletic achievements and inspirational life.
articles.description: The former European champion and two-time Olympic runner had been diagnosed with stage four bowel cancer.

articles.headline: National Stock Exchange reports higher second-quarter profit despite sequential dip
articles.title: NSE Q2 profit rises 23%, but sequential earnings dip 17%
articles.summary: The National Stock Exchange reported a twenty-three percent year-on-year increase in consolidated net profit to two thousand five hundred seventy-seven crore rupees for the quarter ending September. According to the company, total income reached nine thousand eight hundred seven crore rupees for the first half of fiscal year twenty-twenty-seven, driven by higher trading activity. Shares closed higher at one thousand eight hundred three rupees on Tuesday.
articles.description: The bottomline was supported by higher trading activity. Average daily traded volume (ADTV) in the cash market rose 24% YoY to ₹1,18,377 crore in Q2FY27.

articles.headline: Darfur survivors document attacks and mass casualties following Sudan camp fall
articles.title: Darfur survivors vow to tell story of those killed after Sudan camp attacks
articles.summary: Survivors of the Zamzam displacement camp near el-Fasher in Sudan are sharing accounts of violence and starvation following its capture by the Rapid Support Forces in April 2025. A United Nations Human Rights Office report documented at least one thousand thirteen civilian deaths during the assault, while subsequent attacks in the region led to further casualties and widespread displacement.
articles.description: Survivors of attacks on displacement camps in Darfur recall the lives they built, and violence that forced them to flee.

articles.headline: Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel dies following collision with goalkeeper
articles.title: Spanish footballer dies after collision with keeper
articles.summary: Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel passed away on November 3, 2026, after suffering injuries from a collision with FC Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono during a second division match at Heliodoro Rodriguez Lopez stadium. Spanish police launched an investigation into the incident, which occurred with the score tied 2-2. The player experienced a cardiac arrest and subsequent neurological worsening before his death, prompting widespread tributes across the Spanish football community.
articles.description: ‘Broken with pain, with a lump in our throat and unable to believe this is real, CD Tenerife announces the tragic death, at 8:00 a.m., of Jesus de Miguel Alameda,’ his club Tenerife said in a statement.

articles.headline: Vizhinjam port receives first import container, boosting Kerala economic development
articles.title: First import container at Vizhinjam bolsters Keralam’s development aspirations
articles.summary: The Vizhinjam International Seaport marked an operational milestone by receiving its first import container containing building materials from Ningbo, China. Booked by local startup BS2G Logistics and Ship Chandlers for the Alteir Group, the shipment allows Kerala importers to process cargo directly without relying on external ports. Local officials stated that direct import facilities will reduce logistics costs, create employment, and strengthen regional economic development.

articles.headline: Prime Minister Narendra Modi to inaugurate Bengaluru metro Pink Line on November 13
articles.title: Bengaluru’s Pink Line to be inaugurated by Prime Minister on November 13
articles.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi will inaugurate the elevated section of the Pink Line of the Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Ltd. on November 13, 2026, according to Greater Bengaluru Development Minister Krishna Byre Gowda. The launch will push the operational network past 100 km, as authorities aim for 170 km by 2027 to expand public transport.

articles.headline: Anti-Corruption Bureau searches properties linked to MEPMA official Yadagiri Rao Nallaguntla
articles.title: ACB finds ₹4.75 crore assets in searches against MEPMA Additional Director
articles.summary: The Anti-Corruption Bureau registered a disproportionate assets case against Yadagiri Rao Nallaguntla, Additional Director of the Mission for Elimination of Poverty in Municipal Areas, and searched 10 locations on Tuesday. Investigators recovered immovable and movable properties, gold, vehicles, and bank balances, estimating total assets at over ₹4.75 crore before producing him for judicial remand in Hyderabad.
articles.description: Searches at 10 locations uncover properties, gold, silver, vehicles, bank balances and electronic gadgets; the ACB says the market value of these properties is expected to be much higher than their official value

articles.headline: BJP and ABVP hold separate protest marches in Jharkhand targeting opposition parties
articles.title: BJP, ABVP take out marches in Jharkhand, target Congress over democracy, voter list revision
articles.summary: The Bharatiya Janata Party and its student wing Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad held separate protest marches in Jharkhand on Tuesday, accusing the Congress and the INDIA bloc of misleading the public regarding democracy and voter list revisions. Leaders stated that the Special Intensive Revision removes fake entries and protects eligible voters, while criticizing street protests over governance issues.
articles.description: Hundreds of BJP leaders and workers participated in a 'Save Democracy, Remove Anarchy' march led by state BJP president Aditya Sahu

articles.headline: Palghar villagers and opposition leaders continue fierce resistance against Vadhavan port project
articles.title: Vadhavan port project faces continued resistance from Palghar villagers
articles.summary: Villagers, farmers, and fishing communities gathered near Dahanu on Friday to protest the Vadhavan port project, backed by opposition politicians from parties like Congress and Shiv Sena. Protesters warned that the ₹76,220 crore initiative by the Jawaharlal Nehru Port Authority and Maharashtra Maritime Board will destroy marine life, displace Adivasi lands, and threaten traditional livelihoods.
articles.description: Opposition parties have joined villagers in Palghar who say the ₹76,220-crore Vadhavan port will take their sea, their farms and their futures

articles.headline: How a Democrat in Michigan rocked the party days before the US midterms
articles.title: How a Democrat in Michigan rocked the party days before the US midterms
articles.description: BBC's Nada Tawfik visited Detroit, Michigan where the party spat unfolded.

articles.headline: Opposition party organiser killed ahead of South Africa elections
articles.title: Opposition party organiser killed before South Africa elections
articles.summary: An organiser for the uMkhonto weSizwe Party was shot dead at his home in South Africa on Monday during a Zoom call. Police are investigating the motive behind the killing, which comes amid heightened political violence ahead of Wednesday municipal elections. President Cyril Ramaphosa recently deployed soldiers to KwaZulu-Natal province, where the opposition party is projected to make significant electoral gains.
articles.description: Police are investigating the motive in murder of MKP coordinator as political killings rise during municipal elections.

articles.headline: HRV Pharma signs definitive agreements to acquire German wholesale firm Phatebo
articles.title: HRV Pharma to acquire German firm Phatebo
articles.summary: Hyderabad-based virtual pharmaceutical enterprise HRV Pharma is purchasing one hundred percent of Germany-based Phatebo from ZeroStack Corporation to expand into finished formulations and secure a licensed operating business in Europe. Phatebo, which generated revenues of approximately three hundred fifty crore rupees in 2025, will retain its name, leadership under Managing Director Martin Lisker, and existing staff in Hilzingen.
articles.description: The acquisition will take it beyond active pharmaceutical ingredients into finished formulations and give it a licensed operating business in Germany.

articles.headline: Bulgaria has its first elected female president
articles.title: Bulgaria has its first elected female president
articles.description: Iliana Iotova has won Bulgaria’s presidential runoff, becoming the country’s first elected female president.

articles.headline: Binance reveals hackers used fake job interviews in record cryptocurrency theft
articles.title: Binance says fake job interviews used as part of $6.3bn crypto hack
articles.summary: Binance revealed that hackers who stole six point three billion dollars utilized fake job interviews and a compromised internal artificial intelligence tool to target engineers. The exchange suspended withdrawals globally before restoring services and cooperating with agencies including the Federal Bureau of Investigation, which attributed the attack to the Democratic People's Republic of Korea.
articles.description: An engineer was contacted through a legitimate job-hunting platform and invited to bogus job interviews with fake company representatives, Binance says.

articles.headline: Cyclone Murasu brings heavy rainfall and waterlogging to Vijayawada city
articles.title: Cyclone Murasu brings 100 mm rain to Vijayawada; roads inundated
articles.summary: Severe Cyclonic Storm Murasu brought roughly one hundred millimeters of rainfall to Vijayawada and surrounding areas on November 3, inundating major roads and prompting the India Meteorological Department to issue a red alert. District Collector G. Lakshmisha declared school holidays and ordered vulnerable residents evacuated as officials monitored potential inflows into the Budameru rivulet regulator.
articles.description: City receives continuous rain after a prolonged dry spell; red alert remains in force until November 4 morning, schools and colleges to remain closed

articles.headline: Trump repeats unverified claims during final midterm campaign rallies
articles.title: Trump leans into Islamophobia and conspiracy in last-ditch campaign rallies
articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump delivered his final travelling campaign speeches on November 1, 2026, in Iowa and Kansas, urging supporters to vote in the upcoming November 3 midterms. Trump repeated unfounded claims regarding Michigan Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed, calling him a jihadist and a member of the Muslim Brotherhood. The rallies also featured attacks on other Democratic figures, discussions of the US-Israel war on Iran, and immigration concerns as polls indicate potential Democratic gains in both states.
articles.description: Trump attacks Muslim politicians Abdul El-Sayed and Ilhan Omar in his two last rallies on the campaign trail.

articles.headline: Congress delegation moves NHRC over poor students selling blood in Prayagraj
articles.title: Poor students in Prayagraj forced to sell blood for coaching fees, Congress tells NHRC
articles.summary: A Congress delegation led by Rajendra Pal Gautam petitioned the National Human Rights Commission seeking intervention regarding disadvantaged students in Prayagraj selling blood to pay annual coaching fees between 1.20 lakh rupees and 1.80 lakh rupees. According to the memorandum citing a media report, aspirants for competitive exams resort to donations multiple times monthly, threatening their health and violating fundamental rights, while the chairperson assured a probe.
articles.description: Students, mostly from rural, low-income families, were selling blood, sometimes two to four times a month, to pay steep coaching fees, besides hostel and mess charges, the party’s memorandum to the NHRC says

articles.headline: Donald Trump holds final weekend rallies across key states ahead of elections
articles.title: Trump makes final campaign push in final weekend before election
articles.summary: Donald Trump campaigned in Florida, Iowa, and Kansas over the weekend to rally support and protect Republican majorities in Congress ahead of Tuesday's midterm elections. Facing voter frustration over rising living costs, the president shifted his focus to attacking Democrats. Meanwhile, forecasting tools and national polls suggest Democrats hold a strong advantage in capturing control of the legislative branch.
articles.description: The US president rallied in states that Republicans previously won - showcasing how tight Tuesday's elections could be in determining control of Congress.

articles.headline: PM Surya Ghar rooftop solar scheme on track to meet target
articles.title: PM Surya Ghar: 1 lakh rooftop solar installations every 4-5 days; target on track, says Joshi
articles.summary: The PM Surya Ghar Yojana is currently completing one lakh rooftop solar installations every six days, according to Union Minister for New and Renewable Energy Pralhad Joshi during the Bharat Renewable Energy Summit and Expo 2026. Joshi expressed confidence that the residential solar programme will achieve its goal of one crore installations by March 31, 2027, utilizing a utility-led aggregation model to drive the expansion across beneficiaries.
articles.description: At present, the PM-Surya Ghar has about 65.65 lakh beneficiaries and has scaled more than 55 lakh installations.

articles.headline: Independent voters surge as record spending defines midterms
articles.title: US midterms: What to know about independent voters and candidates
articles.summary: Nearly half of United States adults identify as politically independent ahead of the November 3, 2026, midterms, according to the Pew Research Center. Despite this demographic shift, independent candidates face severe financial barriers in an electoral cycle projected to surpass billions in ad spending. While major parties dominate, pollsters note that independent voters could prove decisive in determining the balance of power in Congress and state legislatures.
articles.description: Despite a record number of independents, third-party candidates and voters struggle to penetrate the two-party system.

articles.headline: Kimi Antonelli becomes Formula One's youngest world champion
articles.title: Kimi Antonelli becomes Formula One’s youngest world champion in Mexico City
articles.summary: Mercedes driver Kimi Antonelli secured third place at the Mexico City Grand Prix on November 1, 2026, to become Formula One's youngest world champion at 20 years and 68 days old. Red Bull driver Max Verstappen won the red-flagged race at the Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez, while Ferrari driver Lewis Hamilton finished second. Antonelli's historic victory makes him the first Italian champion since Alberto Ascari in 1953, pushing his overall lead to an unassailable 119 points.
articles.description: Italian wonderkid wins drivers' championship at 20 years and 68 days, finishing third at the Mexico City Grand Prix.

articles.headline: Seventeen-year-old Rudresh donates organs after fatal accident in Thiruvananthapuram
articles.title: 17-year-old Rudresh from Thiruvananthapuram donates organs, offering six people a new lease of life
articles.summary: Following brain stem death caused by a motor vehicle accident, seventeen-year-old Rudresh S.R. saved six lives through organ donation approved by his parents, B. Suresh and P. Remya Devi. Medical teams retrieved both kidneys, pancreas, liver, corneas, and abdominal vessels for awaiting patients at medical institutions including KIMSHEALTH, while the Kerala State Organ and Tissue Transplant Organisation coordinated the retrieval processes.
articles.description: Following the consent given by the family, Rudresh’s both kidneys, pancreas, liver, both corneas, and the abdominal fascia and vessels were harvested

articles.headline: Congress demands election chief resignation over parliamentary debate challenge
articles.title: Congress asks Amit Shah to secure CEC’s resignation before debating the SIR in Parliament
articles.summary: The Indian National Congress party responded on November 3, 2026, to Home Minister Amit Shah by demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and the suspension of the SIR process as preconditions for a special parliamentary session. The political clash followed a rally by the opposition INDIA bloc in New Delhi, during which Shah challenged Congress leader Rahul Gandhi to debate election and delimitation issues in the house.
articles.description: Congress’s communications chief Jairam Ramesh responds to a challenge issued by the Home Minister to Rahul Gandhi for a debate on the SIR, EVMs, and allegations of ‘infiltration’

articles.headline: Gujarat High Court stays order striking down non-vegetarian food ban
articles.title: What is the non-veg ban around Somnath Temple about? | Explained
articles.summary: A Division Bench of the Gujarat High Court stayed a single judge ruling that had previously quashed a government notification banning non-vegetarian food sales near the Somnath temple. Chief Justice Manash Ranjan Pathak and Justice Nirzar Desai issued the stay following an urgent appeal filed by the Gujarat government, ensuring the Gir Somnath District Collector notification remains in force.
articles.description: A Division Bench of Chief Justice Manash Ranjan Pathak and Justice Nirzar Desai stayed Justice Nisha Thakore’s judgment striking down a State government notification banning the sale of non-vegetarian food in the vicinity of the Somnath temple, following an urgent appeal by the Gujarat government

articles.headline: Telangana health department issues public health advisory amid El Nino conditions
articles.title: Telangana issues public health advisory amid El Nino conditions, urges safe water use and heat precautions
articles.summary: The Telangana health department published a public health advisory warning residents about El Nino weather patterns expected to bring dry spells, extreme temperatures, and water shortages. Directed by Public Health and Family Welfare head Dr. B. Ravinder Nayak, the advisory outlines precautions including boiling drinking water, avoiding peak afternoon outdoor work, and following dietary measures to prevent illnesses across public facilities.

articles.headline: Warsaw airports resume normal operations following security checks after bomb threats
articles.title: Bomb threats disrupt operations at Warsaw airports
articles.summary: Polish authorities reported that two Warsaw-bound flights faced bomb threats on November 3, 2026, forcing security inspections and temporary closures at Chopin and Modlin airports. An SAS Scandinavian Airlines flight and a LOT Polish Airlines flight landed safely without incident, and subsequent searches by security personnel found no explosive devices, allowing both facilities to quickly resume their normal operations.
articles.description: The bomb warnings targeted an SAS Scandinavian Airlines flight from Copenhagen and a plane from London’s Heathrow airport operated by Polish airline LOT

articles.headline: Apple reports record revenue while expanding artificial intelligence strategy
articles.title: Apple is all in on AI — its own and everyone else’s
articles.summary: Apple posted its best fiscal year for revenue and earnings per share, with chief financial officer Kevan Parekh highlighting artificial intelligence as a key driver for future growth. The technology giant maintains lower capital expenditures than peers by combining on-device processing and outside services, spending two billion dollars last quarter while anticipating subscription revenue from advanced server features.
articles.description: Apple's latest earnings show how it's continuing to capitalize on the AI boom without busting its budget on the infrastructure spending consuming its competitors. Overall, Apple posted its best-ever fiscal year for revenue and earnings per share. iPhone and Mac sales continued to grow strongly in the fourth quarter. iPhone revenue rose 17.5% from a […]

articles.headline: Nordic nations refuse to play Russia in ice hockey world championships
articles.title: Nordic nations refuse to face Russia in ice hockey World Championship
articles.summary: Denmark, Norway, and Sweden announced they will refuse to play against Russia at the ice hockey world championships next year, following a similar decision by Finland. The move comes after the Court of Arbitration for Sport ruled that Russia must be admitted following an appeal, opposing the stance of the International Ice Hockey Federation.
articles.description: Denmark, Norway and Sweden join Finland in refusing to face Russia in 2027 World Championships in Germany next May.

articles.headline: Venezuelan army attack on Colombian rebel camp leaves 19 dead
articles.title: At least 19 dead in Venezuela army attack on Colombian rebel camp
articles.summary: At least 19 people were killed during a Venezuelan military attack on a National Liberation Army camp in the western state of Apure, according to an NGO and a military source. The operation, which took place on October 30, 2026, targeted the Colombian guerrilla group with drone and helicopter strikes supported by United States intelligence.
articles.description: Juan Francisco Garcia, a coordinator with the group, said on November 1 that “Ten bodies” had been transported to the state capital, San Fernando, the day after the attack

articles.headline: Cyclone Murasu makes landfall in Prakasam district causing widespread damage and evacuations
articles.title: Cyclone Murasu leaves trail of destruction in Prakasam district; no casualties reported
articles.summary: Cyclone Murasu crossed the coast between Kothapatnam and Chinaganjam with wind speeds reaching 120 kilometres per hour. Prakasam District Collector P. Raja Babu reported that authorities relocated over two thousand residents to safety, including dozens of pregnant women who underwent successful deliveries. Strong winds uprooted numerous trees, disrupted electricity and mobile networks, and caused extensive waterlogging without any human casualties.
articles.description: Severe winds and heavy rainfall uproot hundreds of trees, damage electricity poles and disrupt mobile networks, while several livestock were reported dead; officials shift people to relief shelters, including 137 pregnant women

articles.headline: Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay launches bank credit linkages for women in Erode
articles.title: Vijay launches ₹1,110-crore bank credit linkages for 9,000 SHGs in Erode
articles.summary: Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay inaugurated bank credit linkages worth eleven billion ten crore rupees for nine thousand women's self-help groups at Perundurai in Erode district. Organised by the Tamil Nadu Corporation for Development of Women, the event featured the distribution of livelihood assistance and skill development orders. Thousands of security personnel were deployed along the route as massive crowds welcomed him.
articles.description: This is part of a State-wide initiative to extend ₹3,000 crore in bank credit to 26,000 SHGs to promote women’s entrepreneurship. The Chief Minister also distributes livelihood assistance and issues sanction orders for skill development programmes

articles.headline: Alliance partners secure sweeping victory across urban local bodies in Godavari districts
articles.title: Sweeping victory for Jana Sena, TDP in Godavari districts
articles.summary: The coalition of Jana Sena, the Bharatiya Janata Party, and the Telugu Desam Party achieved a resounding electoral success over the Yuvajana Sramika Rythu Congress Party across all five urban local bodies in East and West Godavari districts. Key municipal chairmanships were won by candidates including Jyothi Murala in Nidadavolu, Vegulla Ajay Kumar in Mandapeta, Kottapalli Sailaja in Narsapuram, and Nilofer Shaik in Akiveedu Nagar Panchayat.

articles.headline: Kimi Antonelli secures Formula 1 world championship in Mexico
articles.title: Kimi Antonelli becomes youngest F1 champion; Max Verstappen wins in Mexico
articles.summary: Italian driver Kimi Antonelli secured his maiden Formula 1 world championship on November 2, 2026, at the Mexico City Grand Prix after finishing third behind Max Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton. At 20 years and 68 days old, the Mercedes driver surpassed Sebastian Vettel as the youngest champion in the sport's history, while Verstappen claimed victory in the race with a time of 2 hours, 20 minutes and 28.772 seconds.
articles.description: Antonelli ‌celebrated his first F1 world championship at 20 years and 68 ‌days old, ⁠more than three years younger than Germany’s Sebastian Vettel when ⁠he set the previous record in 2010

articles.headline: Palestine Action protest tactics spread from UK to global offshoots
articles.title: From Italy to Canada, how the UK’s Palestine Action group went global
articles.summary: Activist groups inspired by the British organisation Palestine Action have targeted weapons manufacturers in countries including Italy, France, and Canada by spray-painting facilities and staging occupations. The direct-action movement aims to disrupt global supply chains supporting Israel's military. While the UK proscribed Palestine Action as a terrorist organisation in July 2025, leading to thousands of arrests, international offshoots continue staging protests and intercepting cargo ships.
articles.description: The banned UK group, which targets Israel's war machine, has inspired activists in Europe and beyond.

articles.headline: Cyber attacks strike Russia and Ukraine following truce conclusion
articles.title: Cyber attacks hit Russia, Ukraine after truce ends
articles.summary: Russia reported a massive cyber attack on its public emergency warnings application on November 2, 2026, hours after Ukraine suspected similar hostile interference in its air raid alert system. The digital disruptions occurred as the longest truce of the conflict, which was limited to the Kherson region and brokered by United States First Lady Melania Trump, officially concluded on November 1, 2026, following Russian refusal to extend the pause.
articles.description: The cyber attacks came as the longest truce of the war, limited to Ukraine’s eastern Kherson region, ended on November 1, 2026 after Russia refused the offer of an extension, according to Kyiv

articles.headline: Cyberattacks target supermarket refrigeration systems across Europe and United States
articles.title: Very cold war: Who’s attacking Europe’s supermarket freezers?
articles.summary: Internet-linked refrigeration units at supermarkets across several European countries and the United States were targeted by cyberattacks that raised internal temperatures and spoiled large quantities of food. The incidents affected retailers such as Delhaize, Carrefour, Coop, and IKEA, alongside military bases in Arizona and Rhode Island. Authorities and cybersecurity experts note that vulnerable, internet-accessible controllers were exploited, though no group has claimed responsibility for the disruption.
articles.description: Cold stores in supermarkets across Europe have been targeted in a cyberattack with no clear culprit.

articles.headline: Air India aims to expand widebody fleet and cut costs
articles.title: Air India eyes more widebodies, cost cuts under new CEO
articles.summary: Air India plans to increase its widebody aircraft order while focusing heavily on cost reduction to achieve profitability as soon as possible, according to CEO Tewolde Gebremariam at the Aviation India Summit 2026. The carrier currently has 80 widebody planes on order out of 570 total aircraft ordered in 2023 and 2024 following privatisation. The fleet expansion aims to help the full-service airline regain market share from competitors like Gulf carriers.
articles.description: “Efficiency, efficiency, efficiency,” Air India CEO Tewolde Gebremariam said of the airline’s approach to costs, adding that he was “impatient to see profitability as soon as possible”

articles.headline: Cyber-attacks hit supermarket freezers across ten European countries
articles.title: Europe on alert after supermarket freezers hit by cyber-attacks in 10 countries
articles.summary: Supermarket chains across at least ten European countries experienced a wave of cyber-attacks that raised refrigeration temperatures and forced retailers to discard spoiled food. European Union officials warned of deliberate disruptions to the food supply chain, while national agencies launched investigations. Officials in countries including Italy, Belgium, and Ireland reported varying impacts, and the United Kingdom cybersecurity authorities urged retailers to update vulnerable temperature control software.
articles.description: Supermarkets have reported problems from Estonia and Sweden to Portugal and Italy and many retainers have been forced to discard food.

articles.headline: Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva stages political turnaround in Brazil election
articles.title: Brazil elections | Historic win, humongous challenges
articles.summary: Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva staged a remarkable political turnaround after trailing Flavio Bolsonaro by 45.2 to 47 percent at the end of the first round of Brazil presidential elections, which saw an abstention rate of 21 percent. Thousands of students and workers subsequently marched across urban centers like Niteroi and Rio de Janeiro in widespread protests against Bolsonarism, marking the return of the Left to the streets after more than a decade.
articles.description: Lula tweaked his campaign’s message, speaking more about reducing working hours, relief for indebted families and higher welfare payments under the Bolsa Familia scheme

articles.headline: National Transportation Safety Board investigates fatal private jet crash in Florida
articles.title: Jet may have broken apart before Florida crash, officials say, as family named among victims
articles.summary: The United States National Transportation Safety Board announced that a Learjet 60 may have broken apart in the air before crashing onto a highway in Palm Beach, Florida, on Sunday. The accident resulted in nine fatalities, including technology entrepreneur Adam Robinson, his family, and two crew members, while severe weather and a water-filled impact crater complicated recovery efforts.
articles.description: Adam Robinson, Helen Sharp, and their two children - Emma, four, and Charlie, two - died after the plane nosedived.

articles.headline: Bangladesh garment workers clash with police as minimum wage protests continue
articles.title: Bangladesh garment workers clash with police, defy call to end protests
articles.summary: Paramilitary forces deployed in industrial suburbs around Dhaka on November 3, 2026, as garment workers demanding higher wages defied calls to return to factories. Protesters clashed with police, resulting in numerous injuries and property damage. Workers demand a monthly minimum wage of 30,000 taka to combat high inflation, while authorities claim political agitators are inciting the ongoing unrest.
articles.description: Paramilitary forces have been deployed in Gazipur and Narayanganj as workers demanding a 30,000-taka minimum wage stay on the streets for a fourth day, with 58 police officers injured, the police said

articles.headline: Thousands gather at Ramlila Maidan in Delhi for INDIA bloc rally
articles.title: ‘You can break a stick, not a bundle’: Thousands turn up for INDIA bloc rally from across the country
articles.summary: Supporters from across India arrived in Delhi on November 1, 2026, to attend the opposition INDIA bloc rally at Ramlila Maidan. Attendees voiced concerns over electoral roll revisions, healthcare, and education. Leaders alleged that authorities attempted to block travel, while participants sought political change and revival ahead of upcoming elections.
articles.description: Citizens, youth groups, farmers and political party workers gather ahead of the Ramlila Maidan rally, saying a united movement is needed to fight alleged vote theft and electoral roll irregularities

articles.headline: New bodycam video shows aftermath of fatal National Guard shooting
articles.title: New bodycam video shows aftermath of fatal National Guard shooting
articles.description: Newly-released bodycam footage shows Tennessee National Guard members pointing their guns at 20-year-old Tyrin Johnson.

articles.headline: Congress chief Mallikarjun Kharge attacks Prime Minister Narendra Modi at rally
articles.title: ‘Remove Modi to save democracy’: Congress chief Kharge attacks PM at INDIA bloc rally
articles.summary: Indian National Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge alleged on November 1, 2026, that Bharatiya Janata Party governments at the Centre and in multiple states were formed on stolen mandates. Speaking at an opposition INDIA bloc rally at Ramlila Maidan in New Delhi, Kharge accused Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Home Minister Amit Shah of shielding Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar to disenfranchise marginalized citizens.
articles.description: Addressing INDIA bloc's rally at Ramlila Maidan on the "vote chori" charge, Mr. Kharge also accused Prime Minister Modi and Home Minister Amit Shah of shielding Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar

articles.headline: Qatar remains hopeful the US and Iran can reach a deal
articles.title: Qatar remains hopeful the US and Iran can reach a deal
articles.description: Qatar’s foreign ministry spokesperson Majed al-Ansari says regional neighbours and international partners are working to

articles.headline: Florida governor Ron DeSantis shapes state's 2026 midterm election race
articles.title: How Florida Governor Ron DeSantis will shape his state’s 2026 midterm race
articles.summary: Outgoing Florida Governor Ron DeSantis leaves office due to term limits, having transformed the state from a swing region into a Republican stronghold during his two terms. Political experts state that his hardline conservative legacy and policies will heavily influence the upcoming midterm race. Republican candidate Byron Donalds is campaigning to maintain party control, facing competition from centrist Democrat David Jolly in the election.
articles.description: The outgoing governor and former presidential candidate has transformed Florida into a conservative policy vanguard.

articles.headline: State Bank of India reports fourteen percent profit rise in second quarter
articles.title: SBI Q2 profit rises 14.3% to ₹23,038 crore; eyes NIM above 3%
articles.summary: State Bank of India announced a fourteen percent increase in net profit to twenty-three thousand thirty-eight crore rupees for the quarter ended September 30, 2026. Chairman C.S. Setty attributed the growth to lower loan-loss provisions, improved asset quality, and better liability management which helped maintain the net interest margin above three percent.
articles.description: “In case there is any further repo action, EBLR portfolio further gets repriced quickly. This will add maybe 4-5 basis points to NIM,” Mr. Setty said.

articles.headline: Binance reimburses customers following the largest cryptocurrency hack in history
articles.title: How did Binance recover quickly from the biggest crypto hack in history | Explained
articles.summary: Binance fully replaced over six billion dollars stolen from customer accounts during a major cyber attack on October 29, 2026. The exchange reported that preliminary investigations indicate a compromised engineer laptop allowed the unauthorised withdrawals. The company successfully mitigated customer losses within days while the search for the culprit continued.
articles.description: The largest cryptocurrency exchange in the world was hit by an approximately $6.3 billion hack, the biggest in history, yet customers got their crypto back in about 3-4 days

articles.headline: Eluru district collector orders evacuations as heavy rain inundates low-lying areas
articles.title: Cyclone Murasu: rains inundate low-lying areas in Eluru district; Collector orders evacuation
articles.summary: Incessant rain driven by Cyclone Murasu inundated low-lying areas, uprooted trees, and caused waterlogging across Eluru district on November 3, 2026. District Collector K. Vetri Selvi directed officials to evacuate vulnerable residents and monitor river water levels. Meanwhile, disaster response teams deployed rescue operations as authorities urged citizens to avoid hazardous locations during the severe weather event.
articles.description: Trees uprooted and roads waterlogged as heavy rain lashes several mandals; officials monitor river levels, schools and power lines as rescue teams swing into action

articles.headline: National Human Rights Commission issues notices over alleged minor girl trafficking
articles.title: NHRC issues notice in alleged trafficking of minor girls to Maharashtra
articles.summary: The National Human Rights Commission took suo motu cognisance of media reports on November 3, 2026, alleging minor girls from Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan were sold to middlemen and trafficked to Maharashtra. The commission issued notices to chief secretaries and police chiefs, demanding detailed reports within two weeks regarding the human rights violations and illegal sales involving impoverished families.
articles.description: The girls were trafficked and sold from the border districts of Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan to various cities in Maharashtra; human rights body takes suo motu cognisance of media reports

articles.headline: Supreme Court asks Calcutta High Court to consider Abhishek Banerjee plea
articles.title: Supreme Court grants liberty to Abhishek Banerjee, asks Calcutta HC to consider plea against media trial
articles.summary: The Supreme Court instructed the Calcutta High Court to hear a petition filed by Lok Sabha Member of Parliament Abhishek Banerjee concerning alleged media trials and selective investigative leaks. His counsel argued that trial details shared with media outlets violated his rights. The High Court will reopen after a holiday break.
articles.description: A Bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana said that Abhishek Banerjee can mention for hearing the matter on the reopening of the High Court

articles.headline: Gunmen shoot dead two police officers guarding polio teams in Pakistan
articles.title: Two police officers protecting polio workers in Pakistan shot dead
articles.summary: Unknown attackers on a motorcycle killed two police officers and injured a third in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province while they traveled to protect vaccination staff. Pakistani President Asif Ali Zardari condemned the incident. The violence coincided with a nationwide immunization drive targeting twenty-four million children across ninety-seven districts.
articles.description: The attackers, travelling on a motorcycle, opened fire on a police car in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province.

articles.headline: Israeli election results stand despite Netanyahu voter fraud claims
articles.title: Israeli officials say results stand as Netanyahu claims election ‘stolen’
articles.summary: Israel's Central Elections Committee head Noam Sohlberg stated that general election results will remain valid despite foreign interference claims. Prime Minister Benyamin Netanyahu accused Arab-led parties of stealing the vote with Qatari funding. Meanwhile, opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot alleged Netanyahu is attempting to delegitimise the outcome, while President Isaac Herzog prepares to nominate a government leader.
articles.description: Election body says deadlocked result won't be undermined even if foreign interference claims are found to be true.

articles.headline: Madhya Pradesh police widen illicit liquor smuggling probe into neighboring Gujarat
articles.title: Cop killed in hit-and-run: MP police widen probe to Gujarat in search of absconding driver
articles.summary: Madhya Pradesh police expanded an investigation into a bootlegging ring after an officer was killed during a vehicle interception. Authorities arrested three individuals and deployed a team to Gujarat to track the absconding truck driver. Officials also suspended three liquor shop licenses and three excise department personnel following the incident.
articles.description: Police have arrested three persons, including the alleged kingpin of a bootlegging ring

articles.headline: Telangana Women Commission demands police reports on illegal egg harvesting racket
articles.title: Telangana Women’s Commission seeks reports from police on illegal egg harvesting racket
articles.summary: The Telangana State Commission for Women requested detailed action reports from police commissioners regarding an illegal human egg collection syndicate exploiting vulnerable women. The commission highlighted health risks from hormonal injections and demanded information on rescued victims, registered cases, and potential involvement of medical fertility centers.

articles.headline: Tamil Nadu nodal agency Guidance faces accusations of immobilization from former leaders
articles.title: What is the controversy about Guidance, Tamil Nadu’s nodal agency for investments? | Explained
articles.summary: Guidance, the nodal agency for investment promotion in Tamil Nadu, has drawn criticism after former Chief Ministers M.K. Stalin and Edappadi K. Palaniswami accused the government of immobilizing the organization. Established in July 1992, the non-profit society is mandated to attract investment proposals, facilitate projects, and support the state's economic goals. The body plays a crucial role in the administration's objective to develop the state into a one point five trillion dollar economy by 2036.
articles.description: Guidance, earlier known as the Tamil Nadu Guidance and Export Promotion Bureau, was established as a non-profit registered society on July 15, 1992, with the objective of attracting investment proposals into Tamil Nadu

articles.headline: Al Jazeera journalist recounts arrest during Israeli raid on his home
articles.title: Al Jazeera journalist recounts arrest during Israeli raid on his home
articles.description: Released Al Jazeera Arabic correspondent Montaser Nassar describes how Israeli forces raided his home and arrested him.

articles.headline: French prosecutors launch attempted murder probe over petrol bomb attack
articles.title: France launches attempted murder investigation after petrol bomb thrown at police
articles.summary: French prosecutors initiated an attempted murder investigation after incendiary devices were thrown at police during demonstrations in Paris.
