Interior Minister Laurent Nunez condemned the attack, which injured fifteen officers, including one with severe burns. Authorities recorded over seven hundred arrests during nationwide youth-led protests over the weekend concerning the high cost of living.
articles.description: There were hundreds of arrests as protesters took to the streets in cities across France for the third weekend in a row.

articles.headline: Navy Chief Admiral Swaminathan stresses importance of defense self-reliance
articles.title: Need to build a Navy that can fight, sustain without any constraints: Admiral Swaminathan
articles.summary: Speaking at the Delhi Defence Dialogue on November 3, Indian Navy Chief Admiral Krishna Swaminathan emphasized that self-reliance is a strategic necessity for national security. The event was hosted by the Manohar Parrikar Institute for Defence Studies and Analyses. Swaminathan highlighted geopolitical tensions, the vulnerability of global supply chains, and the critical need to bolster research, development, and indigenous capabilities within the armed forces.
articles.description: The Navy chief emphasised that Aatmanirbharta doesn’t mean isolation, and pitched for collaborating with friendly foreign countries “from a position of strength, and not from a position of weakness”

articles.headline: Anthropic plans European artificial intelligence consultancy venture with Hg
articles.title: Anthropic’s new consulting venture: Why are AI model companies moving into the services business? | Explained
articles.summary: Artificial intelligence developer Anthropic has reportedly partnered with private equity firm Hg to establish an independent consultancy in Europe. Expected to commence operations by the end of 2026 with hubs in London and Berlin, the venture will embed artificial intelligence consultants inside businesses to support technology adoption and serve companies within the Hg investment portfolio, according to a report published on November 3.
articles.description: AI companies are moving into work traditionally handled by consulting and IT services firms, raising questions about who will control enterprise customer relationships and capture revenue from AI implementation

articles.headline: India maintains strict ban on dairy and genetically modified product imports
articles.title: India has never allowed import of genetically modified products, will never open dairy sector: Piyush Goyal
articles.summary: Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal stated during an address at Kirori Mal College in Delhi that India has never permitted imports of genetically modified products or opened its dairy sector in free trade agreements. Goyal emphasized protections for domestic farmers and religious sensitivities regarding animal-derived rennet, while highlighting export targets and manufacturing growth initiatives for the country.
articles.description: Addressing students of Kirori Mal College in Delhi, Piyush Goyal said India has never compromised on any sensitive item and has always protected its farmers, fishermen, and MSMEs in trade pacts

articles.headline: Global elections in Brazil, Serbia and Israel yield diverse outcomes
articles.title: The Lula moment: Polls, promise, precarity
articles.summary: Recent international elections brought significant political shifts, including Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva winning Brazil's presidential runoff. In Serbia, a student-led movement ended Aleksandar Vucic's right-wing populist party rule on October 25, 2026. Meanwhile, Israel's October 27 election resulted in a fragmented parliament that left Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu struggling to maintain his political survival.

articles.headline: Kerala Public Service Commission faces Crime Branch probes
articles.title: Kerala PSC under the scanner: How allegations of examination irregularities have triggered multiple Crime Branch probes
articles.summary: The Kerala Public Service Commission is facing intense scrutiny following allegations of examination irregularities and evaluation lapses. A Special Investigation Team headed by Inspector General of Police S. Ajeetha Begum is currently examining multiple recruitment complaints originating from unevaluated answer sheets discovered during examinations conducted for senior posts.
articles.description: What began with the discovery of unevaluated answers in a 2023 examination for senior posts in the State Planning Board has snowballed into a wider investigation by the Crime Branch

articles.headline: Who decides the US midterms?
articles.title: Who decides the US midterms?
articles.description: About half of all eligible voters in the US skip the midterms. AJLabs looks at who votes and who stays home.

articles.headline: Prime Minister Modi inaugurates Pune Metro Line 3 and outlines expansion
articles.title: PM Modi launches Pune Metro projects, says India’s metro network increased from 248 km to 1,200 km in 12 years
articles.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi stated on Tuesday that India's operational metro network expanded from 248 kilometers in 2014 to 1,200 kilometers across 26 cities. Speaking via video conference for the Pink Line launch in Pune, he laid foundation stones for Phase-II projects worth approximately 21,800 crores. Modi emphasized that enhanced urban transit infrastructure directly improves citizen convenience and accelerates national economic growth.
articles.description: The Prime Minister inaugurated Pune Metro Line 3 (Pink Line) and laid the foundation stone of four new metro corridors under Phase-II, via video conferencing

articles.headline: Kerala UDF government prepares to overhaul state liquor policy
articles.title: UDF poised to recast LDF’s ‘permissive’ liquor policy as it prepares to promulgate it on November 30
articles.summary: The Congress-led United Democratic Front government subcommittee intends to revise permissive State Excise rules established by the previous Left Democratic Front administration before releasing its new framework on November 30. Excise Minister M. Liju stated that the political executive will reclaim authority from deputy commissioners regarding bar licenses. Officials note the policy must balance state revenue needs with public health concerns in Kerala.
articles.description: Excise Minister M. Liju told The Hindu that the UDF would “dismantle the rules and amendments” that gave deputy excise commissioners the power to grant bar licenses

articles.headline: Researchers propose reverse game theory to control artificial intelligence models
articles.title: How “reverse game theory” could keep AI agents in check
articles.summary: Safety researchers are exploring mechanism design, also known as reverse game theory, to align advanced artificial intelligence models by incentivizing adherence to rules rather than peering into internal mechanisms. Proposed approaches include cross-checking model predictions, competitive dynamics, and role-playing auditor and solver systems, though experts note that reliance on rational behavior remains a potential limitation for artificial intelligence applications.
articles.description: A new approach known as “reverse game theory” aims to control powerful AI models by designing systems that incentivize them to stick to the rules. As AI models become more capable, safety researchers are scrambling to ensure they are “aligned” with human desires—to make sure, in other words, that rogue agents don’t break the law,…

articles.headline: Marc Marquez claims Malaysian MotoGP victory to near world title
articles.title: Marquez wins in Malaysia to stand on brink of MotoGP world title
articles.summary: Ducati star Marc Marquez secured a dominant victory at the Malaysian MotoGP in Sepang, finishing ahead of Pedro Acosta and Alex Marquez. The thirty-three-year-old Spaniard expanded his championship lead to forty-four points over Jorge Martin, who missed the race with a wrist injury. Marquez can clinch his eighth world title at the upcoming event in Qatar.
articles.description: Marquez, who is now 44 points ahead of his closest rival Jorge Martin, has seven victories to his name this season

articles.headline: Tamil Nadu Minister Rajmohan alleges five crore rupee bribe offer for post
articles.title: I was offered ₹5 crore to make someone Iyal Isai Nataka Mandram president: Tamil Nadu Minister Rajmohan
articles.summary: Tamil Nadu Minister for Information and Publicity Rajmohan alleged on November 1, 2026, that he was offered a five crore rupee bribe through Tamil Nadu Textbook Corporation chief Layola Mani to appoint an unspecified person as president of the Iyal Isai Nataka Mandram. Speaking in Chennai, the Minister stated he rejected the offer and instead appointed singer Pushpavanam Kuppusamy to the role, prompting All India Anna Dravida Kazhagam leader D. Jayakumar to demand legal action against the briber.
articles.description: According to him, for the first time in Tamil Nadu, every Minister in the Cabinet hates bribery and corruption

articles.headline: DMK seeks vigilance inquiry into Minister Rajmohan's bribery allegations
articles.title: DMK seeks DVAC inquiry into Minister Rajmohan’s allegation of being offered bribery for post
articles.summary: The Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam legal wing joint secretary I. Paranthamen filed a complaint with the Directorate of Vigilance and Anti-Corruption on November 2, 2026. The complaint seeks a First Information Report regarding an alleged five crore rupee bribe offered to School Education Minister A. Rajmohan for a cultural board presidency. The petitioner alleged the Minister and Loyola Mani concealed evidence of the offense.
articles.description: ‘The Minister did not report the offer to the DVAC or any other law enforcement agency; he made it public only on November 1, without disclosing the identity of the person who made the offer,’ said I. Paranthamen

articles.headline: Excise department bar license approvals create friction for Kerala government
articles.title: Excise department’s 'hasty granting' of bar licenses wrong-foots UDF government
articles.summary: Recent bar license approvals by the Kerala Excise Department based on legacy rules have generated political friction for the Congress-led United Democratic Front administration. The opposition Communist Party of India Marxist criticized Excise Minister M. Liju for allegedly failing to preempt the decisions. Liju defended the administration by explaining that previous reforms stripped the political executive of automatic oversight regarding Deputy Commissioner authorizations.
articles.description: The contentious granting of licences, which reportedly angered the UDF’s “prohibitionist base” comprising Christian and Muslim social organisations, occurred as the Cabinet formulated the State’s liquor policy for the current fiscal year

articles.headline: Sudanese allegations of Ethiopian drone attacks expose severe bilateral tensions
articles.title: Deadly RSF drone attacks reveal deep divisions between Sudan and Ethiopia
articles.summary: Sudan lodged formal complaints with the United Nations Security Council and African Union alleging that the Rapid Support Forces launched deadly drone attacks from Ethiopian territory. The allegations highlight deep geopolitical rifts between Khartoum and Addis Ababa, compounded by disputes over the Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam. Analysts warn that an open military confrontation would severely strain the Sudanese military amidst its ongoing domestic conflict.
articles.description: Sudan demands UN accountability after devastating drone attacks expose a complex regional crisis.

articles.headline: Supreme Court of India addresses Delhi traders regarding festive protest disruptions
articles.title: Demonstrations generate ‘protest economy’, Supreme Court tells Delhi traders
articles.summary: The Supreme Court of India heard a petition from the Kirana Committee Delhi concerning business losses caused by prolonged demonstrations during the festive season. A Bench noted the constitutional right to protest alongside the right to livelihood, observing that demonstrations generate localized economic activity for vendors. The court issued notice on the plea without granting immediate interim orders.
articles.description: The Bench expressed sympathy for the right to livelihood of the small traders, hawkers and push cart vendors, noting that their right competed with the right to expression of the protestors

articles.headline: California voters consider ballot measure to impose state wealth tax on billionaires
articles.title: California could become first U.S. State to tax billionaires' wealth
articles.summary: California voters are considering Proposition 40, a ballot measure proposing a one-time five percent tax on net worth exceeding one billion dollars to replace federal healthcare funding cuts. The proposal has divided Democratic leaders, with Senator Bernie Sanders supporting the measure and Governor Gavin Newsom opposing it over fears of wealthy residents leaving the state.
articles.description: Proposition 40 would impose a one-time 5% tax on the wealth of Californians whose net worth exceeds $1 billion, with most of the revenue dedicated to replacing federal funding cuts to healthcare

articles.headline: Andhra Pradesh coastal belt faces continuous heavy rainfall and flash flood alerts
articles.title: Cyclone Murasu: Very heavy rainfall continues to pound Bapatla, flash flood alerts issued
articles.summary: The India Meteorological Department issued flash flood warnings for several districts in Andhra Pradesh as Severe Cyclonic Storm Murasu continued to generate severe gales and very heavy rainfall on November 3, 2026. Bapatla district recorded rainfall exceeding 150 millimeters, prompting the state disaster management authority to maintain active alerts across multiple coastal and interior regions.
articles.description: The A.P. State Disaster Management Authority has warned that very heavy rainfall is likely in the districts of Polavaram, Kakinada, NTR, Krishna, Bapatla, and Palnadu as the Severe Cyclonic Storm is yet to weaken

articles.headline: Lebanese Ministry of Energy cuts electricity supply to public institutions
articles.title: Lebanon cuts power to public bodies as electricity crisis deepens
articles.summary: The Lebanese Ministry of Energy and Water initiated electricity disconnections for approximately one hundred public institutions with unpaid bills, marking an escalation in Energy Minister Joe Saddi's dispute with the government. The action unfolds amid chronic power shortages, economic contraction, and ministerial boycotts of cabinet meetings regarding funding and structural reforms in the energy sector.
articles.description: Political disputes and war worsen Lebanon's electricity crisis, as experts say deeper reforms are necessary.

articles.headline: Suvendu Adhikari accuses opposition leaders of fighting to protect illegal immigrants
articles.title: Mamata, Rahul fighting for infiltrators to keep them in India: Bengal CM
articles.summary: West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari accused Congress leader Rahul Gandhi and former Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee of conspiring to protect illegal immigrants in India. Speaking at Bagdogra airport in Siliguri on Tuesday, Mr Adhikari stated that the central government and the Election Commission of India are working to remove infiltrators. He also criticized Ms Banerjee for participating in a recent opposition rally in Delhi while neglecting local political events in West Bengal.
articles.description: "The ECI and the Centre have taken up the task of driving out infiltrators from the country, whereas Mamata Banerjee and Rahul Gandhi are fighting together to keep them in India," says Mr. Adhikari

articles.headline: Kherson truce ends after evacuation of civilians from Oleshky
articles.title: Kherson braces for return of war as localised Russia-Ukraine truce ends
articles.summary: A six-day localized ceasefire in Ukraine's Kherson region expired without extension or violations on Sunday night, following a joint evacuation operation that relocated hundreds of civilians from Oleshky. According to Ukrainian and Russian officials, ongoing strikes continued across multiple regions, leaving hundreds of thousands of households without power and causing casualties, including a fatal drone attack in Vinnytsia.
articles.description: Moscow and Kyiv continue strikes elsewhere, but no reported violations in Kherson region during the six-day ceasefire.

articles.headline: Tenerife forward Jesus de Miguel dies following on-field collision
articles.title: Tenerife’s Jesus de Miguel dies after on-field collision with goalkeeper
articles.summary: Jesus de Miguel died following a collision with Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono during a Spanish second division match on Monday. The thirty-year-old Tenerife forward sustained severe injuries near midfield seven minutes into added time at Estadio Heliodoro Rodriguez Lopez. The match was abandoned after the red card. According to Spanish media, he suffered a cardiac arrest in an ambulance en route to Hospital Universitario de Nuestra Senora de Candelaria.
articles.description: Tenerife forward Jesus de Miguel suffered a cardiac arrest after a keeper's challenge in Spanish second division match.

articles.headline: Russian strikes cut power across Ukraine as Kherson evacuation truce ends
articles.title: Russian strikes cut power to thousands in Ukraine as Kherson ceasefire ends
articles.summary: Russian strikes on energy infrastructure across four regions left hundreds of thousands of homes without power as a humanitarian ceasefire in the Kherson region expired on Sunday night. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky reported extensive damage and ongoing repairs. Meanwhile, a separate strike in the Vinnytsia region killed two people, and Ukraine retaliated by hitting a missile fuel producer in Russia's Rostov region.
articles.description: A rare humanitarian ceasefire allowed civilians to evacuate the Russian-occupied city of Oleshky.

articles.headline: Thousands displaced from Hebron as Israel carries on siege
articles.title: Thousands displaced from Hebron as Israel carries on siege
articles.description: Almost 5,000 people have been displaced as a result of Israel’s military siege on the city of Hebron in the West Bank.

articles.headline: India records 29% decline in third-quarter gold demand
articles.title: India's gold demand down 29% in July-September at 162.5 tonnes: World Gold Council
articles.summary: India's gold demand dropped 29 percent year-on-year to 162.5 tonnes in the July to September quarter of 2026 due to soaring prices, higher import duties, and official appeals, according to the World Gold Council. Total demand value rose 3 percent to 2,41,900 crore rupees, while jewellery demand fell 20 percent to 99.9 tonnes. The council projects full-year demand between 625 and 675 tonnes.
articles.description: Total jewellery demand in India dipped by 20% to 99.9 tonnes as compared to 125 tonnes in the same quarter of 2025, while in value terms it was up 16% at ₹1,48,700 crores

articles.headline: Sudanese returnees face severe infrastructure challenges in Khartoum
articles.title: Sudan’s displaced return to new challenges in war-battered Khartoum
articles.summary: Mohamed Mahdi Makki Farah and millions of other displaced Sudanese are returning to Khartoum following military declarations freeing the state from Rapid Support Forces. Returnees encounter destroyed homes, high rental costs, and scarce public services. According to United Nations reports, millions have returned despite damaged infrastructure, water shortages, and limited employment opportunities, prompting local authorities to implement emergency measures for public transport.
articles.description: The capital was one of the first areas to be affected, and one of the worst hit, by the war between the SAF and the RSF.

articles.headline: Immigration raids impact California congressional race and farmworkers
articles.title: Surging ICE raids shadow final weeks of California congressional race
articles.summary: Federal immigration enforcement operations by the Trump administration in California's Central Valley have intensified economic and political anxieties during the final weeks of the race for the 22nd congressional district. Democratic challenger Randy Villegas and labour leaders criticise the aggressive tactics, while Republican incumbent David Valadao defends the actions. Community officials report widespread fear among residents, affecting daily routines and local businesses ahead of the November election.
articles.description: Local organisations and representatives say immigration raids have spread fear and uncertainty through communities.

articles.headline: India and Pakistan World Cup match attracts record ticket demand
articles.title: Cricket World Cup: India vs Pakistan gets more ticket requests than final
articles.summary: The International Cricket Council received nearly 8.5 million ticket requests for the upcoming group stage match between India and Pakistan at the 2027 Cricket World Cup in South Africa. The fixture surpassed demand for the tournament final, which received eight million applications. The tournament will feature fifty-seven matches across twelve venues in South Africa, Zimbabwe, and Namibia from October 7 to November 21, 2027.
articles.description: ICC receives 8.4 million ticket requests for 34,000 seats at the October 10 group stage match in Johannesburg.

articles.headline: Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel dies after match collision
articles.title: Tenerife striker De Miguel dies after on-field collision
articles.summary: Jesus de Miguel died following a collision with FC Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono during a Spanish second-division match. The thirty-year-old Tenerife forward suffered head and chest injuries during added time on Monday. Although initially described as stable, his condition deteriorated and he died on Tuesday morning. The incident prompted the Spanish football federation to postpone scheduled cup fixtures, while football clubs and officials expressed widespread grief.
articles.description: Tenerife forward Jesus de Miguel dies aged 30 after an on-field collision during a Spanish second-division match.

articles.headline: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney discusses trade future with Donald Trump
articles.title: Canada PM Carney says he had good conversation with Trump on trade
articles.summary: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney announced on Sunday that he held discussions with United States President Donald Trump regarding future bilateral trade arrangements. Writing on the social media platform X, Carney stated that negotiating teams will work in the coming weeks to deliver a mutually beneficial agreement following months of escalating tariffs between the two neighboring countries.
articles.description: Canada and the United States have ⁠slapped billions of dollars in tariffs on each other in ‌recent months

articles.headline: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney signals progress in United States trade discussions
articles.title: Carney signals progress on Canada-US trade deal talks as midterms loom
articles.summary: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney announced positive progress toward a future trade agreement with the United States on Sunday, just two days prior to the United States midterm elections. Bilateral ties have experienced significant strain due to billions of dollars in mutual tariffs enacted during an escalating trade war between the two North American nations.
articles.description: Canadian PM Mark Carney announces progress in Canada-US trade deal talks ahead of Tuesday's US midterm elections.

articles.headline: Bulgarian President Iliana Iotova leads presidential runoff exit polls
articles.title: Bulgarian President wins runoff election: exit polls
articles.summary: Bulgarian President Iliana Iotova is projected to win Sunday's presidential runoff vote, according to exit polls showing her receiving between 50.7 and 52.5 percent. The election occurred amidst security concerns in European Union and North Atlantic Treaty Organization member states following recent drone attacks on commercial vessels in the Black Sea. Iotova faces Andrey Gyurov, a banker backed by the pro-Western opposition.
articles.description: The vote took place amid security concerns in the EU and NATO member states following a series of drone attacks on commercial vessels in the Black Sea

articles.headline: Goa government to challenge Bombay High Court order on tribal population figures
articles.title: ST seat reservation: Goa to move Supreme Court against High Court order stalling the process
articles.summary: The Goa government plans to file a Special Leave Petition in the Supreme Court by Wednesday to challenge a Bombay High Court interim order that stalled the identification of Scheduled Tribe population figures. The High Court had restrained the Census Commissioner from notifying estimates used to reserve four assembly constituencies for the 2027 polls. A state delegation traveled to New Delhi on Monday to pursue legal remedies after the ruling created uncertainty over the political reservation process.
articles.description: The Panaji Bench of the HC had last week restrained the Census Commissioner from notifying ST population estimates, observing that such figures could not be determined on any basis other than the first official Census conducted after 2026

articles.headline: Acting President Iliana Iotova leads exit polls in Bulgaria runoff
articles.title: Initial results indicate victory for Iotova in Bulgarian presidential vote
articles.summary: Bulgaria acting President Iliana Iotova led the presidential election runoff with just over half the vote on Sunday, according to three exit polls reported by the Bulgarian Telegraph Agency. The election took place while twenty-one people remained missing following Black Sea drone attacks last month. Iotova competed against Andrey Gyurov, a banker and former caretaker prime minister who criticized her stance on Russia.
articles.description: Acting President Iotova would become nation’s first elected female head of state if official results confirm her win.

articles.headline: India faces New Zealand in first one-day international with depleted pace attack
articles.title: IND vs NZ first ODI: New Zealand’s focus on ‘Ro-Ko’ as depleted pace attack a worry for India
articles.summary: India will rely heavily on fast bowler Mohammed Siraj and experienced batters during the opening one-day international against New Zealand in Auckland on November 4, 2026. Due to upcoming Test matches and injuries, India fields an inexperienced bowling attack led by captain Shubman Gill, while New Zealand captain Mitchell Santner manages an aging squad eyeing the 2027 World Cup.
articles.description: With Jasprit Bumrah being preserved for Test matches and the duo of Prasidh Krishna and Harshit Rana still some weeks away from an international return, workhorse Mohammed Siraj will have to shoulder additional burden during the series

articles.headline: Donald Trump and Benjamin Netanyahu discuss Iran war strategy on call
articles.title: Trump holds call with Netanyahu over state of Iran war: report
articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu discussed ongoing negotiations and military strategy regarding Iran during a phone call on Saturday, according to media reports citing American and Israeli officials. Netanyahu reportedly urged immediate strikes following United States midterm elections, while Trump preferred allowing negotiations to continue as Washington balances its military campaign with diplomatic efforts.
articles.description: The Israeli source described the call as “tough,” while the American source said it was “direct,” according to Axios

articles.headline: North Korea denies involvement in record 6.3 billion dollar Binance cryptocurrency hack
articles.title: North Korea denies being behind record $6.3bn Binance hack
articles.summary: North Korean official Kim Yo-jong dismissed allegations linking Pyongyang to a record 6.3 billion dollar hack of cryptocurrency exchange Binance as a sinister US provocation. While US agencies and blockchain analysts blamed the state-backed TraderTraitor group, Binance resumed trading after covering most losses and experiencing 3.6 billion dollars in customer withdrawals.
articles.description: US government agencies and cyber analysts have blamed Pyongyang for the record-breaking heist.

articles.headline: Indian-origin candidates contest across United States midterm elections
articles.title: Who are the Indian-origin candidates in U.S. midterm elections?
articles.summary: Numerous individuals with South Asian heritage are running for public office in the November 2026 legislative contests across various American states. Prominent incumbent lawmakers and new nominees are seeking positions in Congress, state executive offices, and local governments. These campaigns encompass multiple jurisdictions, highlighting the growing political participation of this community within the American electoral system.
articles.description: Democratic lawmakers Ro Khanna, Pramila Jayapal, Ami Bera and Suhas Subramanyam are seeking re-election to the U.S. Congress

articles.headline: Aligarh Muslim University holds first student union elections in eight years
articles.title: AMU wants women on campus, not at the ballot box
articles.summary: Aligarh Muslim University in India has launched its first student union elections in eight years. Male candidates wearing traditional black sherwanis campaigned on campus lawns for the Aligarh Muslim University Students Union vote. During campaigning, female students questioned candidates regarding their exclusion from voting rights at the university ballot box.
articles.description: Around 4,000 women students at AMU’s Women’s College have been denied voting rights in the Aligarh Muslim University Students’ Union (AMUSU) elections, raising concerns over gender discrimination and unequal representation. Their fight to be included in the university-wide electoral process has brought renewed scrutiny to the separate-union rules and the barriers women face in campus politics, finds A. M. Jigeesh

articles.headline: Telangana issues red alert for three districts due to cyclone Murasu
articles.title: Cyclone Murasu Nov. 3 | Red alert lifted from two Telangana districts; issued for Suryapet, Khammam and Bhadradri
articles.summary: Three districts in Telangana were placed under red alert for extremely heavy rain on November 3, 2026, as severe cyclonic storm Murasu crossed the Andhra Pradesh coast, according to the India Meteorological Department. The IMD forecast heavy to very heavy rainfall in Suryapet, Khammam, and Bhadradri Kothagudem districts, while lifting the warning for Nalgonda and Nagarkurnool. Meanwhile, Mahabubabad received an orange alert.

articles.headline: High Court begins hearings on legal challenge to Australia child social media ban
articles.title: Major test for Australia's social media ban begins in High Court
articles.summary: Australia's High Court has commenced two days of hearings regarding a constitutional challenge against the national social media ban for children under sixteen. Filed by the Digital Freedom Project and supported by platform Reddit, critics argue the legislation violates rights to free communication and privacy. The policy, introduced last December, requires ten major platforms to take reasonable steps to prevent underage access or face significant financial penalties.
articles.description: Lawyers for Reddit and a digital rights group are arguing the world-leading policy robs children of their right to free communication.

articles.headline: Audit highlights heavy drinking water financial burden on poor Bengaluru families
articles.title: Audit flags ₹3,000 monthly drinking water burden on poor families in Bengaluru
articles.summary: Economically weaker families in Bengaluru spend around 3,000 rupees monthly on private water tankers due to an impending drinking water crisis caused by a monsoon deficit, according to preliminary water audit findings by the Water Satyagraha campaign. Campaign convenor Syed Ahmed Hussain stated that poor households spend more on water than the state government's monthly assistance, while the city faces a projected shortfall exceeding 600 million litres daily.
articles.description: The city extracts groundwater at nearly twice the rate at which it is replenished and loses about 400 million litres of piped water every day, according to Syed Ahmed Hussain, convenor of the Water Satyagraha campaign

articles.headline: Two helicopters crash near Everest base camp, killing Indian tourist
articles.title: Two helicopters crash near Everest base camp, killing Indian tourist
articles.description: Two helicopters have collided while preparing to land in Nepal’s Mount Everest region, killing an Indian tourist.

articles.headline: Morocco celebrates as UN Western Sahara mission ends after US-Russia dispute
articles.title: Why a US-Russia showdown left Morocco celebrating
articles.summary: Morocco welcomed the conclusion of the United Nations peacekeeping mission in Western Sahara after the Security Council failed to renew its mandate on October 31, 2025. A United States proposal backing Moroccan autonomy was vetoed by Russia, while a rival Russian draft also failed. The expiration of the mission leaves the future of Africa's longest territorial dispute uncertain.
articles.description: An impasse between the US and Russia at the UN means its peacekeeping mission in Western Sahara has ended after 35 years.

articles.headline: US midterm election results timing depends on state voting methods and close races
articles.title: When will we know the US midterm election results?
articles.summary: United States midterm elections begin closing polls on Tuesday, with results expected to trickle in over days depending on the state. While some states like Florida report quickly, others using mail-in or ranked-choice voting, such as Alaska and California, may take days or weeks. Control of both chambers of Congress remains uncertain as news organisations analyse vote counts.
articles.description: The first results are expected on Tuesday as polls begin to close at 23:00 GMT. But final results might take days.

articles.headline: Historical roots of One Health connect human, animal and environmental medicine
articles.title: The cow, the flea and the genome: One Health and the statecraft of prevention
articles.summary: Historical precedents for the One Health approach date back to Emperor Ashoka in the third century BCE, who provided medical care for both people and animals. Rudolf Virchow later coined the term zoonosis to emphasise the lack of division between animal and human medicine, linking environmental and biological health across centuries.
articles.description: A cattle virus at home and a plague scare abroad make the same argument this World One Health Day: life is epidemiologically indivisible, and the institutions that govern and study it must learn to be so too

articles.headline: Helicopter crash near Mount Everest base camp leaves one person dead
articles.title: One dead after two helicopters collide near Mount Everest in Nepal
articles.summary: A helicopter collision near Mount Everest base camp in Pheriche village resulted in the death of a forty-seven-year-old Indian national and injured two others on Tuesday, according to authorities. The accident occurred at an altitude of 4,200 metres as both aircraft attempted to land. The region relies heavily on helicopters for transport due to a lack of roads.
articles.description: Authorities have confirmed that a 47-year-old Indian national was killed and two people injured.

articles.headline: Reserve Bank of India resumes urban cooperative bank licensing after twenty-two years
articles.title: After 22 years, RBI reopens UCB licensing: can new audit rules ensure a safer banking sector? | Explained
articles.summary: The Reserve Bank of India has resumed urban cooperative bank licensing after a 22-year hiatus. The policy shift occurs as authorities seek to implement stricter audit rules and regulatory guardrails to prevent past governance failures and ensure greater stability within the cooperative banking sector moving forward.
articles.description: MSC​​ARO and ICAI build guardrails for multi-state cooperatives aspiring to become banks

articles.headline: India and Israel oppose UN draft on conventional arms control
articles.title: India, Israel vote against UNGA draft on regional conventional arms control
articles.summary: India and Israel voted against a United Nations General Assembly draft resolution concerning regional conventional arms control, proposed by Pakistan and Belarus. Speaking at the UN, First Secretary Anmol Sher Bedi stated that India opposes addressing security concerns solely within regional boundaries and questioned the necessity of the UN Disarmament Commission starting from scratch.
articles.description: India and Israel were the only countries to vote against the resolution in the 193-member UN body

articles.headline: Iran war becomes central issue ahead of US midterm elections
articles.title: How will the Iran war shape the outcome of the US midterm vote?
articles.summary: The conflict with Iran has emerged as a major campaign issue ahead of United States midterm elections on Tuesday, November 3, as voters grapple with skyrocketing fuel prices and inflation. Polls indicate that voters from both major political parties question the consequences of the war, potentially impacting the balance of power in the Senate and House of Representatives for President Donald Trump.
articles.description: The conflict has become a central issue ahead of Tuesday's polls.

articles.headline: Australia high court hears legal challenge against under-sixteen social media ban
articles.title: Australia’s High Court hears bid to overturn under-16s social media ban
articles.summary: Australia's social media ban for users under sixteen is facing a legal challenge in the High Court brought by Reddit and the Digital Freedom Project. The challengers argued the restriction has limited effectiveness and restricts political discourse. According to the eSafety Commissioner, restrictions aim to protect young users from online predators and graphic content.
articles.description: Online giant Reddit and advocacy group Digital Freedom Project argue ban is unconstitutional.

articles.headline: Union Health Ministry proposes ten new import gateways
articles.title: Centre proposes 10 new import gateways for drugs, medical devices
articles.summary: The Union Health Ministry has proposed amending Rule 43A of the Drugs Rules of 1945 to add 10 inland container depots, a Special Economic Zone, and Noida International Airport as authorised entry points for importing drugs, medical devices, and cosmetics. According to the ministry, this expansion aims to reduce inland transportation distances, optimise logistics costs, and improve supply chain efficiency across India.
articles.description: The proposed amendment to Rule 43A of the Drugs Rules, 1945, is aimed at easing import operations, reducing inland transportation distances and improving the movement of healthcare products across the country

articles.headline: Asian Football Confederation reschedules 2027 tournament due to regional conflict
articles.title: AFC reschedules Asian Cup 2027 in Saudi Arabia amid regional conflict
articles.summary: The Asian Football Confederation announced on Tuesday that the 24-team Asian Cup 2027 in Saudi Arabia has been postponed from January to December 23, 2027, concluding on January 21, 2028. Governing body officials stated that the rescheduling was necessary due to logistical complexities and travel disruptions arising from ongoing regional conflicts, including missile and drone attacks targeting Saudi territory.
articles.description: Start date for AFC Cup 2027 moved from January to December due to ongoing Houthi attacks on host nation Saudi Arabia.

articles.headline: German cost-of-living protests turn violent with looting and arrests
articles.title: Peaceful protests in Germany spiral into violence and looting
articles.summary: Demonstrations across Germany regarding living costs escalated into violence and looting in Frankfurt, Berlin, Cologne, and Hamburg. German authorities confirmed that at least 54 people faced arrest and more than 100 police officers sustained injuries during the unrest. The protests were initially organised by the campaign group Gen Z regelt before deteriorating into widespread civil disorder.
articles.description: Thousands joined largely orderly demonstrations earlier in the day, before violence erupted in Frankfurt, Berlin, Cologne and Hamburg.

articles.headline: Indian Navy rescues hijacked fishing vessel and twenty crew members off Somalia
articles.title: Indian Navy rescues hijacked fishing vessel off Somalia, frees all 20 crew members
articles.summary: The Indian Navy successfully rescued the hijacked fishing vessel Azini off the northeastern coast of Somalia after a 48-hour operation, securing all 20 crew members. The operation involved a mission-ready warship, reconnaissance aircraft, and Marine Commandos deployed via an Indian Air Force C-17 aircraft to neutralize the armed pirate group without casualties.
articles.description: The operation demonstrated the Navy’s operational preparedness and its ability to undertake complex maritime security missions through seamless coordination with the Air Force

articles.headline: US Senator Dan Sullivan vows to accept election outcome
articles.title: Sullivan vows to honour Alaska race outcome, US judge dismisses DOJ lawsuit
articles.summary: Republican incumbent Dan S. Sullivan promised to respect the upcoming November 3 midterm election results in Alaska. A federal judge dismissed a Department of Justice lawsuit seeking to decertify the race over a spoiler candidate controversy. Sullivan accused his Democratic opponent Mary Peltola of cheating, while Peltola denied any campaign involvement in recruiting the independent candidate.
articles.description: Senator Sullivan's pledge contrasts with the Trump administration's effort to challenge Alaska's election certification.

articles.headline: Indian Navy plans futuristic warships under Project 18A
articles.title: What is Project 18A, and why is the Navy embarking on building futuristic warships? | Explained
articles.summary: The Indian Navy has received in-principle approval from the Defence Acquisition Council, chaired by Defence Minister Rajnath Singh, for Project 18A to develop next-generation stealth guided-missile destroyers. Estimated at around 80,000 crore rupees, the programme aims to build larger and more heavily armed warships to address emerging maritime threats and enhance India's power projection across the Indo-Pacific region.
articles.description: The Indian Navy is preparing for a major transformation of its surface combat fleet with Project 18A, an ambitious programme to develop next-generation stealth guided-missile destroyers

articles.headline: Israel establishes diplomatic ties with Somaliland through ambassador exchange
articles.title: Israel’s first ambassador to Somaliland presents credentials in Hargeisa
articles.summary: Israel’s first ambassador to Somaliland, Michael Lotem, presented his credentials to President Abdirahman Mohamed Abdullahi in Hargeisa following a diplomatic agreement reached on December 26, 2025. Somaliland declared independence from Somalia in 1991. Somalia President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud challenged the move, alleging Israel seeks access to the Red Sea. The recognition was condemned by Somalia, the Arab League, the African Union, and the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation.
articles.description: Israel expands ties with the breakaway territory as Somalia challenges its motives and war intensifies in Yemen.

articles.headline: Indian national killed in helicopter collision in Nepal
articles.title: Indian killed as two helicopters collide in Nepal
articles.summary: A 47-year-old Indian national was killed and another passenger injured when two helicopters operated by Fishtail Air and Air Dynasty collided while landing on November 3, 2026, in Nepal's Solukhumbu district. According to police, the incident occurred at Pheriche near Mount Everest Base Camp, leading to the airlift of injured individuals to Kathmandu for medical treatment.
articles.description: The number of passengers aboard the two helicopters at the time of the collision has yet to be confirmed

articles.headline: Indian national killed, another injured as two helicopters collide in Nepal’s Solukhumbu
articles.title: Indian national killed, another injured as two helicopters collide in Nepal’s Solukhumbu

articles.headline: US midterm campaigns intertwine foreign policy with domestic economic pressures
articles.title: Foreign policy is a local issue in U.S. midterm campaigns
articles.summary: As Americans prepare to vote in midterm elections on November 3, foreign policy matters have merged with domestic concerns. According to an Associated Press study, competitive congressional campaigns heavily featured the war in Iran and trade tariffs, linking international conflicts directly to rising living costs for voters.
articles.description: The number of Republicans who say that Trump’s policies have made the economy worse has almost doubled (18% to 35%) since the start of the year

articles.headline: U.S. midterm elections decide control of Congress
articles.title: What are U.S. midterm elections?
articles.summary: Midterm elections held nationwide halfway through a presidential term determine control of all four hundred thirty-five House seats and roughly one third of the Senate. The November 3 vote serves as a referendum on the administration, impacting legislative power, foreign policy, and immigration rules while remaining crucial for upcoming presidential races.
articles.description: The U.S. midterm elections on November 3 determine control of Congress, with all 435 House seats, about one-third of the 100 Senate seats, and numerous state governorships up for grabs, in a nationwide vote that weakens or strengthens the President’s agenda depending on which party prevails.

articles.headline: CITU announces indefinite protest at Jantar Mantar in Delhi
articles.title: Over one lakh workers expected at Jantar Mantar in Delhi for indefinite protest by CITU starting December 1
articles.summary: The Centre of Indian Trade Unions will launch an indefinite protest at Jantar Mantar in New Delhi on December 1, 2026, demanding the repeal of labour codes and the protection of workers' rights. CITU State unit president S. Varalakshmi stated that over one lakh workers are expected to participate, highlighting concerns over unorganised sector wages, safety, and rising worker suicides.
articles.description: The Centre of Indian Trade Unions (CITU) will launch an indefinite protest at Jantar Mantar demanding protection of workers’ rights and repeal of ‘anti-worker’ labour codes

articles.headline: Andhra Pradesh chief minister orders urgent measures as cyclone Murasu approaches
articles.title: Cyclone Murasu: A.P. CM calls for efforts to prevent loss of lives
articles.summary: Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu instructed officials to prioritise public safety and essential supplies as cyclone Murasu made landfall near Ongole. The storm caused widespread waterlogging and power disruptions across several districts. Authorities stated that the weather system was expected to subside by November 3 night, prompting calls for accelerated restoration works in badly affected areas.
articles.description: In a teleconference with senior officials in the State administration, and District Collectors, Mr. Naidu advised the people to follow government advisories till the cyclone withers away

articles.headline: Pakistani physics graduate dies by suicide following Harvard admission fraud
articles.title: How a Harvard dream ended in tragedy for a Pakistani family
articles.summary: Laiba Ijaz, a 24-year-old physics graduate in Islamabad, died by suicide on October 9 after her family was defrauded of millions of rupees by a man promising her admission to Harvard University. The suspect, Muhammad Noman, was arrested and later died in police custody. Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi subsequently handed over recovered funds to the grieving family.
articles.description: A 24-year-old physics graduate dies after her family pays millions to a man who lied about getting her into university.

articles.headline: Severe cyclonic storm Murasu crosses Andhra Pradesh coast near Ongole
articles.title: Cyclone Murasu completes landfall, to weaken by noon
articles.summary: The severe cyclonic storm Murasu crossed the coast near Ongole in Andhra Pradesh, bringing heavy rainfall to multiple districts. According to the India Meteorological Department, the system moved north-northwestwards and was expected to weaken into a cyclonic storm by noon, with wind speeds gradually decreasing. Heavy rainfall was forecasted to persist over South Coastal Andhra Pradesh for twelve hours.
articles.description: Heavy spells of rainfall may likely to continue over South Coastal Andhra Pradesh during next 12 hours, the IMD said

articles.headline: Israeli forces maintain military siege on Hebron for tenth day
articles.title: Hebron siege continues for 10th day as Israel threatens wider offensive
articles.summary: Israeli forces are maintaining their lockdown on Hebron in the occupied West Bank for the tenth consecutive day following an October 23 attack that killed two Israeli soldiers. According to Mayor Yousef al-Jabari, the siege has displaced over 3,300 Palestinians, caused daily economic losses exceeding 3.8 million dollars, and resulted in infrastructure damage. Meanwhile, the United Nations human rights office reported that Israeli settlers carried out 397 attacks across the territory in October.
articles.description: Hebron's economic losses surpass $3.8m as Israeli forces demolish West Bank homes and close hundreds of businesses.

articles.headline: Bombay High Court allows actor Imran Khan to reside in India
articles.title: What did Bombay High Court rule in actor Imran Khan’s ‘Leave India’ notice case? | Explained
articles.summary: The Bombay High Court permitted actor Imran Khan Pal to continue residing in India pending the next hearing on December 7. The ruling followed an unconditional apology and an undertaking not to participate in future protests. However, the court declined to quash the departure notice issued by the Foreigners Regional Registration Officer and sought a detailed response from the Centre.
articles.description: The Bombay High Court observed that the rights of OCI cardholders and Indian citizens operate in distinct spheres. It also acknowledged that the State, in the exercise of its sovereign powers, has the authority to deport a person from India in an appropriate case

articles.headline: Bangladeshi garment workers protest for higher wages amid surging inflation
articles.title: ‘Going hungry’: Garment workers in Bangladesh say wages barely cover needs
articles.summary: Garment workers in Bangladesh staged widespread protests demanding a minimum wage increase to cope with soaring living costs and high inflation. The demonstrations disrupted operations at hundreds of factories and prompted police intervention. In response, the government announced a new wage board, while officials urged demonstrators to return to work as negotiations regarding industry pay began.
articles.description: Tens of thousands of workers in world's second-largest apparel exporter hit the streets to demand better minimum wages.

articles.headline: Abdulla Shahid accuses Mohamed Muizzu of reviving anti-India campaign in Maldives
articles.title: Muizzu could stir up anti-India campaign again: Former Maldives Minister Abdullah Shahid
articles.summary: Former Maldives Foreign Minister Abdulla Shahid accused President Mohamed Muizzu of moving in an anti-India direction ahead of the 2028 presidential elections. Speaking in October 2026, Shahid criticized Muizzu over 20 recent MoUs signed with Pakistan and called for parliamentary transparency. The remarks highlight growing political tensions in the Maldives as opposition figures mobilize against the ruling party.
articles.description: Following Maldivian President Mohamed Muizzu’s Pakistan visit, Abdulla Shahid, running to be a presidential contender in 2028, hits out at Mr. Muizzu, saying the President will ‘try to create some narrative on hate’ before the elections

articles.headline: California cities pass moratoriums on data centres amid surging electricity concerns
articles.title: California’s Bay Area debates data centres ahead of US midterm elections
articles.summary: Several San Francisco Bay Area cities enacted temporary 45-day moratoriums on new data centre construction following public protests over strained power grids and rising electricity bills. The issue has become prominent in Tuesday's midterm elections, with congressional candidates offering contrasting views on artificial intelligence regulation and development. Analysts note that public backlash against rapid technological expansion remains exceptionally high across the region.
articles.description: At least seven Bay Area cities have passed data centre moratoriums, despite the region's reputation as an AI hub.

articles.headline: Israeli strikes in Gaza kill eight people including one child
articles.title: Israeli strikes in Gaza kill eight including child, hospitals say
articles.summary: At least eight people, including a child, were killed in Israeli air strikes across Gaza on November 1, 2026, hospital officials reported. A strike in Gaza City hit civilians near a school, while another in Khan Younis targeted police officers. The attacks occurred despite a year-old ceasefire agreement mediated internationally.
articles.description: Five officers from the Hamas-run police have been killed in Khan Younis and three people, including a child, killed in Gaza City, officials say.

articles.headline: Indian stock markets extend winning streak with Sensex jumping 615 points
articles.title: Stock markets extend rally in early trade; Sensex jumps 615 points
articles.summary: Benchmark indices Sensex and Nifty extended their winning run in early trade on November 3, 2026, driven by foreign fund inflows and declining crude oil prices. The BSE Sensex rose 614.66 points to reach 76,301.63, while the NSE Nifty gained 149.80 points to hit 23,588.55. Experts noted that supportive macroeconomic factors and Q2 results are currently accelerating the ongoing market rally.
articles.description: In Asian markets, South Korea's Kospi and Shanghai's SSE Composite index traded lower, while Hong Kong's Hang Seng index quoted higher

articles.headline: US voters head to polls across 36 states for midterm congressional elections
articles.title: What time do polls open and close in the US midterm elections 2026?
articles.summary: More than 230 million eligible US voters can cast ballots on Tuesday to decide all 435 House of Representatives seats, 35 Senate seats, and gubernatorial races in 36 states. Voting hours vary by state, with Vermont opening the first polls at 5 am and Alaska closing last. Control of Congress hangs in the balance as voters navigate closely watched contests across multiple key states.
articles.description: The first polls are set to open in Vermont at 5am (10:00 GMT).

articles.headline: UK revises immigration rules to double permanent residency wait for workers
articles.title: UK to double wait for permanent residency, with exemptions for care workers
articles.summary: British Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood announced in Parliament that most foreign workers must now wait 10 years to qualify for permanent residency, up from five years. The policy links settlement eligibility to income levels while exempting hundreds of thousands of low-paid care workers from the harshest timelines. Meanwhile, refugees arriving via unauthorized small boats could face a wait of up to 30 years under the overhauled system.
articles.description: Under new rules, most workers will have to wait 10 years to settle in the UK, but higher earners can qualify sooner.

articles.headline: Enforcement Directorate freezes bank account and searches premises over counterfeit medicines
articles.title: ED attaches assets, freezes bank account in counterfeit medicines racket; searches five premises in Bengaluru
articles.summary: The Directorate of Enforcement executed searches across five locations in Bengaluru and froze a bank account holding approximately 9 lakh rupees as part of a money-laundering probe. The investigation follows an August 18 police case regarding an illicit operation that repackaged generic drugs to resemble expensive Pfizer antibiotics for distribution.
articles.description: During the raid, the accused were allegedly found storing medicines and pharmaceutical drugs without valid licences, permits or authorisations and replacing labels on the stored medicines.

articles.headline: Supreme Court lifts blanket ban to allow green firecrackers for Deepavali
articles.title: Why is it difficult to ensure only green firecrackers are burst during Deepavali?
articles.summary: The Supreme Court lifted its blanket ban on firecrackers, permitting the use of green firecrackers for Deepavali just five days before the festival. Activists and historical data indicate that enforcing these regulations will prove challenging, as previous partial and complete bans in the national capital have frequently been flouted by residents over the years.
articles.description: Over the years, both complete or partial bans on firecrackers have been openly flouted by people in the national capital

articles.headline: Russian authorities report drone strike on Nizhny Novgorod industrial enterprise
articles.title: Russia says drone hit 'industrial enterprise' near Moscow, Kyiv claims hit major refinery
articles.summary: A massive overnight drone attack significantly damaged an industrial plant in the Kstovo district of Nizhny Novgorod, according to regional governor Gleb Nikitin on November 1, 2026. Ukrainian media claimed the target was a major oil refinery. The incident follows recent strikes on Russian energy infrastructure amid ongoing conflict.
articles.description: Gleb Nikitin, governor of Nizhny Novgorod region, reported a "massive drone attack" during the night, during which an "industrial enterprise in the Kstovo district sustained significant damage"

articles.headline: Donald Trump campaigns in Iowa and Kansas to support Republican Senate
articles.title: Trump rallies in Iowa, Kansas to maintain Republican control of US Senate
articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump is holding rallies in Iowa and Kansas on November 1, 2026, to help maintain Republican control of the Senate ahead of the midterm elections. The events follow temporary cancellations and come as polls show tight races. Over 52 million Americans have already cast their ballots nationwide.
articles.description: US President Trump returns to the campaign trail after taking a break at his ⁠⁠Mar-a-Lago club in Florida on Saturday.

articles.headline: Address change applications in Telangana lead to unintended voter deletions
articles.title: Telangana SIR: Address change applications at odds with enumeration forms ending up in deletion of voters
articles.summary: Voters across Hyderabad faced accidental deletion from draft electoral rolls during the Special Intensive Revision of Electoral Rolls. Due to delays in processing Form 8 address change applications and confusion regarding enumeration forms, officials categorized affected residents as untraceable without prior notice. As of November 2, 2026, authorities received over one million Form 8 applications across Telangana.
articles.description: Many Form 8 applications for address change were rejected as the electors were deleted from rolls after not being found at the old address during Enumeration Phase

articles.headline: Candidates in Michigan Senate race hold final rallies before election
articles.title: El-Sayed, Rogers hold dueling rallies as bitter campaign comes to a close
articles.summary: Democrat Abdul El-Sayed and Republican Mike Rogers held final campaign rallies in Michigan on November 2, 2026, ahead of the United States Senate midterm elections. The bitter contest received a late surprise when Democratic Representative Haley Stevens endorsed Rogers. A recent New York Times Siena poll indicated El-Sayed led his opponent by 11 percentage points among likely voters.
articles.description: The events come as Haley Stevens opined on why she withdrew support for the US Senate Democratic nominee.

articles.headline: Rahul Gandhi warns Prime Minister and Home Minister of future legal action
articles.title: Gyanesh Kumar will go to jail: Rahul Gandhi
articles.summary: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi asserted at an INDIA bloc rally on November 1, 2026, that Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Home Minister Amit Shah will face legal consequences for alleged electoral irregularities. He also claimed Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar will be jailed for treason, while praising supporters for defending the nation's constitution.
articles.description: At INDIA bloc rally in Ramlila Maidan, LoP says the 2024 mandate for the Modi government was “illegal”; he outlines a post-Narendra Modi vision rooted in inclusivity and harmony

articles.headline: Andhra Pradesh coast prepares for landfall of Cyclonic Storm Murasu
articles.title: Days after Cyclone Arnab, Andhra Pradesh braces for Cyclonic Storm Murasu landfall
articles.summary: Five districts in Andhra Pradesh are under a red alert as Cyclonic Storm Murasu approaches for landfall between Nellore and Narsapur on November 2, 2026. Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu cancelled a Delhi trip to review safety preparations. The storm follows Cyclone Arnab, which caused severe damage and five deaths.
articles.description: Cyclonic Storm Murasu likely to turn into severe cyclonic storm by Monday morning; red alert issued in five A.P. districts; heavy rain also forecast for parts of Tamil Nadu and Odisha

articles.headline: North Korea tests cluster-bomb warheads in latest military drills
articles.title: North Korea tests cluster-bomb warheads in latest weapons drill
articles.summary: North Korea test-fired cluster-bomb warheads on October 31, 2026, to assess tactical ballistic missile combat adaptation. The official Korean Central News Agency reported that the weapon can devastate a target area of 12 to 13 hectares. This test follows previous trials of attack drones and hypersonic missiles amid rising border tensions involving South Korea.
articles.description: It also came against the backdrop of growing tensions over a landmine explosion along the heavily fortified border between the two Koreas that saw three South Korean soldiers wounded

articles.headline: Iran warns renewed conflict with United States could outlast previous war
articles.title: Iran warns new war could last longer after Trump threatens strikes
articles.summary: Iran warned on November 1, 2026, that any future military conflict with the United States could surpass past hostilities in duration. Army spokesman Mohammad Akraminia stated that Washington cannot dictate the timing of its conclusion. The warning follows comments from U.S. President Donald Trump regarding potential strikes on remaining targets and recent diplomatic messages.
articles.description: Diplomatic efforts to end the West Asia war have been punctuated by repeated threats from the U.S. and Israel to resume bombardments as they hold crucial elections

articles.headline: Karnataka Chief Minister directs milk federation to reduce curd prices
articles.title: Amid public backlash, Karnataka Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar directs Karnataka Milk Federation to reduce curd prices
articles.summary: Karnataka Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar instructed Karnataka Milk Federation officials on November 2 to lower recently hiked curd prices following public criticism. The cost per litre had risen from 54 rupees to 68 rupees on November 1, prompting hoteliers and citizens to question the increases implemented to support local farming families.
articles.description: Though the State government has been justifying the price rise, hotel owners and the public have criticised it; prices being reworked and will be released soon, says KMF official

articles.headline: Man and boy arrested in Australia over baseball bat attack on volunteer
articles.title: Man and boy arrested after allegedly attacking One Nation volunteer with bat
articles.summary: Australian police arrested a 37-year-old man and a 14-year-old boy following an alleged baseball bat attack on a One Nation party volunteer in Torquay on October 25, 2026. The volunteer sustained non-life threatening injuries. Victorian One Nation leader Warren Pickering stated the incident occurred after interference with election signs, while Premier Ben Carroll condemned the political violence.
articles.description: The incident comes amid growing calls for the temperature of political debate in Australia to be turned down.

articles.headline: Fire breaks out at HPCL Visakh Refinery with no casualties
articles.title: Fire breaks out at HPCL Visakh Refinery; no casualties reported
articles.summary: A major fire erupted at the Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Limited Visakh Refinery on late November 2, 2026, originating in the Pitch Tower of the Residue Upgradation Facility. Malkapuram Inspector of Police E. Narasimha Rao confirmed that internal fire teams successfully suppressed the blaze without any reported injuries or fatalities. HPCL officials stated that primary processing units remain fully operational.
articles.description: Reassuring the public, Malkapuram Inspector of Police E. Narasimha Rao issued a voice message that the situation was under control

articles.headline: Naftali Bennett's faction endorses Gadi Eisenkot to form new Israeli government.
articles.title: Naftali Bennett’s ‘B’Yachad’ faction throws support behind Gadi Eisenkot to form next Israeli government
articles.summary: Former Israeli Prime Minister Naftali Bennett announced his B’Yachad faction will recommend Yashar party chief Gadi Eisenkot to President Isaac Herzog to form the next government following recent Knesset elections. President Herzog urged political leaders to find creative solutions to resolve the ongoing deadlock after neither main bloc secured a clear majority in the 120-member parliament.
articles.description: The development comes as Israeli President Isaac Herzog has urged political leaders to accept the election results and find creative solutions to prevent another election

articles.headline: Israel's far-right parties retain 13 seats despite high turnout in recent vote
articles.title: Israel’s far-right supporters hold out hope for return to power
articles.summary: Israeli far-right politicians Itamar Ben Gvir and Bezalel Smotrich maintained their combined total of 13 seats in the Knesset election held on October 27, 2026, falling short of expectations for major gains. While supporters in cities like Sderot expressed ongoing backing for their hard-line security positions, political analysts note the faction faces potential marginalization as mainstream parties negotiate the formation of a new governing coalition.
articles.description: After years of the Israeli electorate drifting rightwards under Mr. Netanyahu, far-right parties such as Mr. Ben Gvir’s Jewish Power and Bezalel Smotrich’s Religious Zionism had hoped for watershed gains

articles.headline: UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham open to slavery apology without reparations
articles.title: Burnham ‘open’ to UK slavery apology, but not reparations: Why now?
articles.summary: British Prime Minister Andy Burnham announced openness to apologising for Britain's historical role in the transatlantic slave trade while explicitly rejecting financial reparations. Writing in The Guardian on October 31, 2026, Burnham expressed personal sorrow ahead of a Commonwealth summit in Antigua and Barbuda, contrasting with persistent demands from Caribbean leaders and CARICOM.
articles.description: The UK PM's statement comes as Commonwealth nations meet in Antigua and Barbuda.

articles.headline: What is the role of Legislative Councils? | Explained
articles.title: What is the role of Legislative Councils? | Explained
articles.description: What is the constitutional basis for Legislative Councils in the States? What were the arguments for and against? How are members elected and nominated? What powers do Legislative Councils have in relation to Legislative Assemblies? What reforms did the Second Administrative Reforms Commission propose?

articles.headline: Severe Cyclonic Storm Murasu crosses Andhra Pradesh coast bringing heavy rain
articles.title: Cyclone Murasu brings deluge to parched Prakasam district
articles.summary: Severe Cyclonic Storm Murasu crossed the Andhra Pradesh coast near Kothapatnam on November 3, 2026, dumping heavy rainfall across Prakasam and Bapatla districts and reducing Prakasam's rainfall deficit to 58.6 percent. Naguluppalapadu recorded a maximum of 198.01 mm of rain. The Andhra Pradesh State Disaster Management Authority issued alerts for gale winds and potential storm surges.
articles.description: A red alert is in place for the districts of Tirupati, Nandyal and Palnadu for November 3, 2026 and an orange alert for 11 other districts

articles.headline: India gross GST collections grow 23 percent to over 2.31 lakh crore rupees in October.
articles.title: GST mop-up surges 23% to second-highest level of ₹2.31 lakh crore in October on festive demand boost
articles.summary: Gross Goods and Services Tax collections increased significantly in October 2026, driven by strong domestic activity and rising import revenues, according to government data released on November 1, 2026. Domestic sales revenues and import collections both registered substantial growth. After accounting for annual refunds, net collections also posted a notable double-digit increase for the month.
articles.description: Gross GST collections from domestic sales rose 16% to over ₹1.59 lakh crore, and revenues from imports climbed 42% to ₹72,246 crore

articles.headline: Chief Justice of India calls for strengthening High Court public confidence
articles.title: CJI calls for strengthening public confidence in High Courts
articles.summary: Chief Justice of India Suyra Kant urged authorities to enhance public trust in High Courts during the platinum jubilee celebrations of the Kerala High Court on November 1, 2026. Speaking in Kochi, he emphasized that these institutions must remain accessible to vulnerable populations and transparent in case listings. The event was attended by Union Minister Arjun Ram Meghwal and Kerala High Court Chief Justice Soumen Sen.
articles.description: High Courts should continue to remain accessible to the vulnerable, attentive to the urgency of human suffering, and unwavering in its commitment to constitutional values, says Surya Kant

articles.headline: Chief Minister Naidu reviews cyclone relief as Murasu makes landfall
articles.title: No power disruptions reported as Cyclone Murasu makes landfall near Kothapatnam in Prakasam dist.
articles.summary: Cyclone Murasu made landfall near Kothapatnam in Prakasam district on November 3, 2026, prompting Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu to review the ground situation with district collectors. Energy officials confirmed no power disruptions or fallen electricity poles occurred. District collectors reported clearing fallen trees and shifting vulnerable families to relief camps while preparing for local body election vote counting.
articles.description: During the teleconference, Collectors briefed Andhra Pradesh CM Chandrababu Naidu on the ground situation and relief measures

articles.headline: New study explores how smoking sets the stage for lung cancer
articles.title: How smoking sets the stage for lung cancer | Explained
articles.summary: This article is a partial text or introduction that outlines a scientific conundrum regarding how chronic inflammation from smoking damages lung tissue and increases cancer risk long before definitive mutations take root, without providing further details or study outcomes.
articles.description: Chronic smoke exposure alters lung stem cells and weakens their safety mechanisms and local immune defences, creating a precancerous state; common KRAS and TP53 mutations triggered tumours only in smoke-conditioned tissue, showing how smoking primes cells for cancer

articles.headline: Sixty-six US lawmakers urge Trump administration to halt Afghan deportations
articles.title: US lawmakers ask Trump administration to stop deportation of Afghans
articles.summary: Sixty-six United States lawmakers wrote to Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Department of Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin on November 2, 2026, demanding a halt to the deportation of at least 150 Afghans. Advocacy groups reported a scheduled flight from Louisiana to Pakistan. The deportees include former allies of coalition forces facing severe danger under Taliban rule.
articles.description: At least 150 Afghans are facing deportation to Pakistan and on to Afghanistan.

articles.headline: Israeli attacks on Gaza kill at least nine people
articles.title: Israeli attacks on Gaza kill at least nine people
articles.description: Israeli attacks on Gaza City and Khan Younis killed at least nine people on Sunday.

articles.headline: Supreme Court order on green firecrackers raises implementation and stock concerns
articles.title: Activists raise concern over Supreme Court order on green firecrackers, traders lament stock availability
articles.summary: Environmental activists and traders in Delhi voiced concerns on November 3, 2026, following a Supreme Court order permitting green firecrackers on November 7 and 8. Activists warned of toxic air due to enforcement challenges, while Rajiv Kumar Jain of the Delhi Fireworks Traders Association stated that limited sale windows and short notice make procuring sufficient stocks extremely difficult.
articles.description: Over the years, both complete or partial bans on firecrackers have been openly flouted by people in the national capital

articles.headline: External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar meets counterparts in Atlanta
articles.title: S. Jaishankar meets Russian, Polish, South Korean counterparts; discusses Ukraine, West Asia
articles.summary: External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar held bilateral discussions on October 31, 2026, with Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov, Polish Deputy Prime Minister Radoslaw Sikorski, and South Korean Foreign Minister Cho Hyun. The meetings occurred on the sidelines of the G20 Foreign Ministers' Meeting in Atlanta, focusing on the Ukraine conflict, West Asia, and multilateral ties before attending a college football game.
articles.description: The External Affairs Minister also met Polish Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Radoslaw Sikorski

articles.headline: Israeli military attacks across Gaza kill at least eight Palestinians
articles.title: At least eight Palestinians killed in Israeli attacks across Gaza
articles.summary: At least eight Palestinians were killed in Israeli military strikes across Gaza on Sunday, according to hospital sources. An attack in al-Mawasi targeted police officers, while a drone strike in Gaza City's Rimal neighbourhood killed three people, including a four-year-old child. Hamas condemned the strikes as a war crime, while the Israeli army stated it targeted a terrorist in southern Gaza.
articles.description: Four-year-old among eight Palestinians killed in Israeli drone attacks across the Gaza Strip.

articles.headline: US midterm elections record early voting surge with fifty million ballots
articles.title: More than 50 million votes cast in US midterm elections: What does it mean?
articles.summary: More than 50 million Americans cast early ballots ahead of the November 3, 2026, midterm elections, according to a University of Florida analysis. Early voting turnout surged significantly in states like Texas and South Carolina compared to 2022. The increase follows expanded mail-in and in-person voting options, higher democratic enthusiasm, and voter anxiety surrounding the cost-of-living crisis.
articles.description: A record number of early votes is cast as both parties campaign before Tuesday's polls.

articles.headline: Binance covers ninety percent of losses following massive cryptocurrency hack
articles.title: Crypto firm Binance covers 90% of losses after $6.3bn hack
articles.summary: Cryptocurrency exchange Binance announced on October 31, 2026, that it covered ninety percent of the 6.3 billion dollars stolen in a recent cyberattack. Co-chief executive officer Richard Teng stated that corporate treasury funds were used to protect users, while analytics firms suspect North Korean hackers. Law enforcement and the company are continuing investigations and freezing assets.
articles.description: The Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) says North Korea was responsible for the hack.

articles.headline: Iran and United States explore diplomatic opening amid military threats
articles.title: Iran and US explore diplomacy amid rising threats of war
articles.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi stated that Qatari-mediated talks have created a potential diplomatic opening with the United States, reducing Tehran's Strait of Hormuz reopening offer to two days. However, both nations maintain military readiness as Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei demanded maximum deterrence against potential US and Israeli attacks on infrastructure following prior conflicts.
articles.description: Iran says could reopen Hormuz in shorter period if conditions met, as Trump says US still has targets to 'take care of'.

articles.headline: Ministry of Home Affairs plans Foreigners Regional Registration Offices in all state capitals
articles.title: Foreigners’ registration offices in all State Capitals by 2027: MHA
articles.summary: The Union Ministry of Home Affairs announced on November 2, 2026, that the government intends to establish Foreigners Regional Registration Offices in every state capital by 2027. Directed by Home Minister Amit Shah, the expansion aims to improve immigration services and security enforcement, increasing the total number of operational offices across the country to twenty.
articles.description: Ministry says the expansion is intended to improve access to immigration and consular services, strengthen regulatory compliance, and support India’s efforts to attract international visitors

articles.headline: Samajwadi Party president Akhilesh Yadav expands PDA plank to court upper-caste voters
articles.title: Akhilesh redraws ‘PDA’ to woo upper castes; rhetoric may not be enough, say political analysts
articles.summary: Samajwadi Party president Akhilesh Yadav has expanded his PDA coalition to include Brahmins, Baniyas, and Kayasthas in an effort to fracture the ruling Bharatiya Janata Party base ahead of the upcoming assembly election.
