articles.headline: Amit Shah praises Chandigarh Police on its raising day
articles.title: Amit Shah lauds Chandigarh Police, says it set benchmarks for police forces across country
articles.summary: Union Home Minister Amit Shah lauded the Chandigarh Police on its sixtieth raising day, presenting the force with the President's Colour on November 1, 2026. Shah commended its six decades of service and announced the addition of one hundred forty-one new vehicles to enhance emergency response times, modern policing, and mobility across the northern region.
articles.description: Amit Shah was addressing a gathering on the occasion of the 60th Raising Day event of Chandigarh Police and presenting the President’s Colour to the force

articles.headline: Bulgarian voters cast ballots in presidential run-off amid Black Sea security tensions.
articles.title: Bulgarians vote in presidential run-off amid Black Sea tensions
articles.summary: Citizens are voting in a presidential run-off featuring incumbent Iliana Iotova and former caretaker Prime Minister Andrey Gyurov amid regional security threats. The election follows recent drone attacks on merchant ships off the Black Sea coast. Exit polls will follow the closure of voting at 8pm, with final results anticipated on Monday as candidates address the maritime crisis.
articles.description: Voters in Bulgaria weigh economic challenges and attacks on ships in a race marked by record low turnout.

articles.headline: Is China’s ‘dark tourism’ turning disaster education into entertainment?
articles.title: Is China’s ‘dark tourism’ turning disaster education into entertainment?
articles.description: China is seeing growing interest in ‘dark tourism’, where visitors flock to attractions that recreate natural disasters.

articles.headline: Yemeni forces seize military positions in al-Jawf
articles.title: Yemeni government forces seize strategic positions in al-Jawf
articles.summary: Yemen’s internationally recognised government reported that its forces recaptured military positions and strategic heights east of al-Hazm in al-Jawf governorate. The United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs stated that more than 290,000 people have fled their homes since fighting escalated in August, while the ongoing siege of Taiz continues to severely restrict deliveries of essential food, fuel and medical supplies.
articles.description: Weapons and ammunition depots are seized after a counteroffensive.

articles.headline: Serbia changes government following years of protests
articles.title: From railway tragedy to gov’t change: Serbia’s two-year fight for justice
articles.summary: Serbia experienced a political shift after the Student List opposition movement won the October general election, following months of protests sparked by the collapse of a railway station canopy in Novi Sad that killed 16 people. Longtime leader Aleksandar Vucic resigned as president and pardoned prosecuted activists before his party conceded defeat in the election.
articles.description: A timeline of events since the deadly train station collapse in Novi Sad, which led to a change of government in Serbia.

articles.headline: Marc Marquez wins Malaysian Grand Prix in Sepang
articles.title: Marquez wins Malaysian Grand Prix to close in on retaining championship
articles.summary: MotoGP champion Marc Marquez won the Malaysian Grand Prix at the Sepang International Circuit, extending his championship lead to 44 points over absent rival Jorge Martin. KTM rider Pedro Acosta finished second and Gresini rider Alex Marquez took third place. The Ducati rider can secure his eighth title at the upcoming Qatar Grand Prix.
articles.description: Marc Marquez takes 44-point lead over Jorge Martin and can seal the MotoGP title in Qatar next weekend.

articles.headline: Israeli protesters urge Jewish-Arab coalition government
articles.title: Israeli protesters urge Jewish-Arab coalition government
articles.description: Israeli protesters urge Jewish-Arab coalition government

articles.headline: Four workers die in Ujjain hotel waste chamber
articles.title: Four die of suspected suffocation while cleaning waste chamber in Madhya Pradesh’s Ujjain hotel
articles.summary: Four workers died from suspected poisonous gas and suffocation after entering a food-waste tank at the Shri Ganga Hotel along the Ujjain-Dewas road in Madhya Pradesh. Ujjain Collector Roshan Kumar Singh and Superintendent of Police Pradeep Sharma confirmed that police and hotel staff recovered the bodies by breaking open the chamber following the incident.
articles.description: Two workers collapsed after entering the food-waste tank at Shri Ganga Hotel on the Ujjain-Dewas road; two more entered to rescue them, and all four died

articles.headline: Malawi cattle farmers travel farther for scarce river fodder
articles.title: Malawi cattle farmers travel farther as El Nino worsens drought
articles.summary: Malawi cattle farmers are travelling longer distances to find river grass as prolonged dry spells and El Nino impact southern Africa. In Mulanje, herders and fodder gatherers struggle with depleted vegetation, higher costs for maize bran, and competition from riverbank agriculture. Cooperatives report declining milk production and squeezed earnings as they await upcoming rains to restore pasture.
articles.description: For many families, keeping cattle alive is becoming an increasingly costly struggle.

articles.headline: Record spending drives competitive United States midterm Senate races
articles.title: Where are the most expensive midterm races and who is funding them?
articles.summary: Voters across the United States are preparing for the midterm elections on Tuesday, with control of Congress hinging on expensive Senate races in states like Texas, Ohio, and Michigan. Billionaire donors and political action committees have poured billions into the contests. Republicans have raised more overall, though polls suggest Democrats are favoured to control both chambers.
articles.description: Senate races in Texas, Michigan and Ohio rank among the most expensive in this year's midterm cycle.

articles.headline: Bangladesh forms new wage board to address garment worker protests
articles.title: Bangladesh forms wage board as garment workers protest
articles.summary: Authorities in Bangladesh established a six-member committee to determine a revised minimum wage following demonstrations that disrupted industrial hubs around Dhaka. Demonstrators demanded thirty thousand taka per month, citing soaring living costs. Meanwhile, Ministry of Labour and Employment adviser M Sakhawat Hossain Chowdhury urged employees to resume work as clashes with police injured several people near the capital.
articles.description: Demonstrations held in industrial cities as workers demand wage increase as cost of living rises.

articles.headline: Israeli protesters urge opposition to form coalition with Arab parties
articles.title: Israeli protesters demand opposition ally with Arab parties to oust Netanyahu
articles.summary: Hundreds of demonstrators gathered in Tel Aviv and Jerusalem to demand that Israeli opposition leaders ally with Arab-majority parties to remove Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu from power following an inconclusive election. The proposed coalition could secure sixty-seven seats in parliament, although key opposition figures remain divided over accepting support from Arab factions amid ongoing regional security tensions and political disputes.
articles.description: Arab-majority parties made major gains in elections, fuelled by anger over rhetoric targeting the community from Mr. Netanyahu’s hard-right government, but opposition chief Gadi Eisenkot has not decided whether to seek a coalition with them

articles.headline: Supreme Court clears income tax assessments for former chief justice sons
articles.title: Supreme Court paves way for IT assessments of two businessmen sons of former CJI Y.K. Sabharwal
articles.summary: The Supreme Court dismissed four appeals filed by Chetan and Nitin Sabharwal, allowing income tax reassessment notices issued for assessment years 2008-09 and 2009-10. A bench comprising Justices J.B. Pardiwala and K. Vinod Chandran upheld that the tax department possessed valid reasons to investigate share transactions utilized to acquire a prime property on Delhi's Sikandra Road in 2010.
articles.description: A Bench of Justices J.B. Pardiwala and K. Vinod Chandran dismissed four appeals filed by Chetan and Nitin Sabharwal, while upholding income tax reassessment notices issued for assessment years 2008-09 and 2009-10

articles.headline: Serbia’s canopy collapse, two years on in a changed country
articles.title: Serbia’s canopy collapse, two years on in a changed country
articles.description: Two years after Novi Sad’s railway station canopy collapse, Serbia marks the second anniversary of the tragedy.

articles.headline: Donald Trump states Flavio Bolsonaro can remain in United States
articles.title: Donald Trump says Flavio Bolsonaro can stay in U.S. as long as he wants amid Brazilian probes
articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump announced that defeated Brazilian presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro may remain in the country indefinitely. Speaking in Florida during a Halloween event, Trump criticized Brazil's recent election. Bolsonaro arrived under humanitarian parole following money laundering probes and the revocation of his passport, while U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio engaged with Brazilian diplomats.
articles.description: Flavio Bolsonaro’s decision to go to the U.S. followed a ruling by a Brazilian Supreme Court Justice to revoke his passport shortly after his loss, as the candidate faces a pair of federal money-laundering probes in Brazil and police there considered him a flight risk

articles.headline: Punjab activists demand justice following the murder of Parvinder Singh Jhota
articles.title: In Punjab, the highway to 2027
articles.summary: Protesters in Mansa town maintain a permanent sit-in camp on October 13 following the fatal shooting of anti-drug crusader Parvinder Singh Jhota. The forty-year-old activist was killed in broad daylight, leaving his last rites delayed by a fortnight as demonstrators demand action against the drug menace that has plagued the northern Indian state for over twenty years.
articles.description: The drug menace in Punjab has stayed at the centre of political and social attention over the past decade or more. With the killing of anti-drug crusader Parvinder Singh Jhota, public emotions are running high. Political parties are hoping to capitalise on this, with the Assembly election due in early 2027, finds Vikas Vasudeva

articles.headline: India marks 79 years of independence following map changes
articles.title: How were the States formed and how has the Indian map changed since 1947?
articles.summary: Following the Indian Independence Act of 1947 and the lapse of British paramountcy, India divided into two independent dominions and integrated numerous princely states. As India marks 79 years of independence, the country now contains 28 states and eight Union Territories after decades of internal boundary reorganisations driven by multiple factors.
articles.description: The last transformation of the Indian map happened in 2019 with the creation of the Union Territories of J&K and Ladakh

articles.headline: Portuguese police disperse housing protesters from Lisbon camp
articles.title: Police storm Portugal housing protest camp
articles.summary: Law enforcement officers equipped with shields and batons cleared a tent encampment in Lisbon following a large demonstration against controversial rental legislation. Dozens of police officers moved into Rossio Square to dismantle over fifty tents after issuing warnings regarding illegal encampments. The intervention follows similar police actions that previously sparked criticism and injuries amidst Portugal severe national housing affordability crisis.
articles.description: Dozens of officers, some accompanied by police dogs, moved into Rossio Square in Lisbon early on Sunday.

articles.headline: Two newly elected Bihar independent MLCs extend support to ruling BJP
articles.title: Two newly-elected Bihar Independent MLCs now support BJP
articles.summary: Rahul Raj and Banshidhar Brajwasi extended their support to the ruling Bharatiya Janata Party after winning legislative council elections as independent candidates from Saran Teachers and Tirhut Graduate constituencies. Both individuals previously defeated Janata Dal United candidates. The Bihar BJP formally welcomed the new legislators during a party meeting attended by senior state leaders.
articles.description: Both the Independent candidates, significantly, had defeated the ruling alliance partner Janata Dal-United candidates from their respective constituencies

articles.headline: Depression over Bay of Bengal intensifies into deep depression
articles.title: Depression intensifies into deep depression over Bay of Bengal
articles.summary: A weather system over the southeast Bay of Bengal developed into a deep depression by the early hours of November 1, 2026, according to the India Meteorological Department. Positioned hundreds of kilometres from various coastal cities, the system is projected to evolve into a cyclonic storm over the next six hours and a severe storm by November 2.
articles.description: The system is likely to further intensify into a severe cyclonic storm over the westcentral Bay of Bengal on November 2

articles.headline: US Secretary of State denies helping Flavio Bolsonaro flee Brazil
articles.title: Rubio says Trump administration did not help Bolsonaro flee Brazil to US
articles.summary: United States Secretary of State Marco Rubio stated on Saturday in Atlanta that the administration did not assist defeated Brazilian politician Flavio Bolsonaro in fleeing to the United States. Bolsonaro, who faces corruption investigations in Brazil, arrived in Miami on Wednesday after receiving a visa following his October 25 election loss to President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva.
articles.description: Trump says defeated presidential candidate, who faces investigation in Brazil, can stay in the US 'as long as he wants'.

articles.headline: Canelo Alvarez defeats Christian Mbilli to reclaim WBC super middleweight title
articles.title: Canelo Alvarez defeats Christian Mbilli to reclaim WBC title in Riyadh
articles.summary: Saul Canelo Alvarez secured a 12-round decision victory over French fighter Christian Mbilli in Riyadh on Sunday to recapture his World Boxing Council super middleweight title. The 36-year-old Mexican boxer triumphed in Saudi Arabia despite regional security concerns, earning judges' scores of 115-112, 116-111, and 117-110 to add another belt to his storied professional career.
articles.description: Mexican boxing star wins 12-round decision to defeat the French fighter and regain the super middleweight belt.

articles.headline: Golden State Valkyries defeat Atlanta Dream to capture first WNBA crown
articles.title: Golden State Valkyries defeat Atlanta Dream to capture first WNBA crown
articles.summary: Gabby Williams scored 30 points, including 28 in the second half, to lead the Golden State Valkyries to a 68-63 victory over the Atlanta Dream on Saturday in San Francisco. The win in game seven secured the Women's National Basketball Association championship in the franchise's second season, with Williams earning the Finals Most Valuable Player award.
articles.description: Gabby Williams, named Most Valuable Player, sets records for most points (137) and most steals (18) in the WNBA Finals.

articles.headline: James Talarico challenges Republicans in costly Texas Senate race
articles.title: Democrats are used to heartbreak in Texas - could Talarico turn the tide?
articles.summary: Democratic candidate James Talarico is challenging Republicans in a high-stakes United States Senate race in Texas that has exceeded half a billion dollars in spending. Recent polls indicate a tight contest in the reliably red state, prompting visits from political figures including President Donald Trump. Strategists warn that a potential Democratic victory could significantly alter the political landscape both locally and nationally.
articles.description: The state's $500m Senate race may be the most closely watched in the US midterms, and is about far more than control of Congress.

articles.headline: Vatican confirms Pope Leo XIV cast mail-in ballot in US
articles.title: How can Pope Leo vote in U.S. elections while serving as the sovereign of Vatican City? | Explained
articles.summary: The Holy See Press Office confirmed that Chicago-born Pope Leo XIV, formerly known as Robert Francis Prevost, has cast his vote in the United States midterm elections. The Vatican stated that the pontiff has exercised his right to vote as a United States citizen whenever eligible by submitting his mail-in ballot in Chicago, maintaining a long-standing practice of civic participation.
articles.description: Does becoming the Pope automatically mean giving up American citizenship? Can a foreign head of state retain the right to vote in U.S. elections? How does Pope Leo XIV’s dual status as the sovereign of Vatican City and a US citizen affect his voting rights?

articles.headline: Andhra Pradesh urban local body elections begin under tight security
articles.title: Urban local body elections begin in Andhra Pradesh
articles.summary: Voting for mayors, chairpersons, and ward members across 13 municipal corporations and 79 municipalities and Nagar Panchayats in Andhra Pradesh began at 7:00 am on November 1, 2026. State Election Commissioner Anil Chandra Punetha is monitoring the process amid heavy security deployment, including closed-circuit television cameras and drones, following earlier violence during the nomination filing phase across thousands of sensitive polling stations.
articles.description: State Election Commissioner Anil Chandra Punetha and his team of officers are personally monitoring the conduct of the elections, for which elaborate arrangements were made, including the installation of CCTV cameras and deployment of drones at places where clashes are anticipated

articles.headline: India records below average monsoon despite shaping El Nino
articles.title: Why even a strong El Niño does not guarantee a poor Indian monsoon
articles.summary: The 2026 southwest monsoon concluded nearly thirteen percent below the long term average of eighty seven centimeters, accompanied by a developing El Nino expected to peak in December. East and Northeast India experienced their driest season since records began in 1901. Historically, strong El Nino events do not always guarantee poor monsoon outcomes.
articles.description: Seven Indian monsoons since 1950 have run into a moderate or strong El Niño. Of these, in five years, including 2026, monsoon rainfall levels were at least 10% lower than the long-term average. The IMD refers to this level as 'deficient’. The 2023 season was something of an exception with ‘below average’ rainfall. However, 1997 had ‘average’ rainfall

articles.headline: Tamil Nadu cabinet approves Social Justice Survey
articles.title: How significant is the TVK-led regime’s move to hold Social Justice Survey? | Explained
articles.summary: The Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam-led regime in Tamil Nadu has officially approved the formation of a multi-member panel to conduct a Social Justice Survey. Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay announced the decision during a cabinet meeting in Chennai on October 29, 2026, fulfilling an earlier commitment made by Governor Rajendra Vishwanath Arlekar regarding state demographic data collection.
articles.description: The feature of an ‘open column’, where respondents can state their caste during the second phase of the Census, to be carried out in most parts of the country during February next year, has forced many parties and other stakeholders to express concerns over the utility of the whole exercise

articles.headline: Vehicles torched in Pulivendula hours before municipal elections begin
articles.title: Vehicles torched ahead of polls in Pulivendula
articles.summary: Several vehicles were set on fire in Pulivendula hours before municipal elections commenced on Saturday morning. Police reported that three cars, ten motorcycles, and a tractor were destroyed near Madhusudhan Reddy's orchard. Polling subsequently opened briskly amidst brief clashes and stone pelting between rival cadres, prompting law enforcement intervention across multiple wards in the town.
articles.description: The incident happened around midnight near the orchard belonging to Madhusudhan Reddy, where three cars, ten motorcycles and a tractor were fully burnt

articles.headline: Maharashtra FDA issues strict order to curb expired food sales
articles.title: Maharashtra FDA issues order to curb sale, repackaging of expired food items
articles.summary: The Food and Drug Administration has introduced a mandatory requirement for companies to provide proof of proper disposal and destruction certificates from approved facilities. According to FDA Commissioner Tukaram Mundhe, recent state operations led to two registered cases and the seizure of adulterated goods worth five crore rupees. Authorities also cracked down on illegal activities in Bhiwandi and other regions.
articles.description: Speaking at a press conference in October 30, Mr. Mundhe says that instead of destroying stale and expired food items properly, they are being “disposed of only on paper.” These goods are brought back after being repacked by some agents and then sold to citizens. In some cases, even the production dates are being manipulated

articles.headline: Prime minister Modi highlights historic poverty decline citing World Bank report
articles.title: PM Modi cites World Bank report to highlight ‘historic’ fall in India’s extreme poverty
articles.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi highlighted a World Bank report showing that India recorded one of the world's fastest poverty reductions, with 49.6 crore people moving out of poverty between 2011 and 2023. According to the October 2026 brief, extreme poverty plummeted from 27.1 percent to 2.6 percent, while employment grew by 13.4 crore in six years. Modi contrasted his administration's targeted efforts with past opposition campaigns during the announcement on Instagram.
articles.description: In a post on Instagram featuring the inspiring and energetic song ‘Thaan Liya’ from the Bollywood movie ‘Dasvi’ as background music, Mr. Modi highlighted that the “historic" drop in poverty represents a generational surge in opportunities

articles.headline: INDIA bloc stages Chalo Dilli march to demand election commissioner resignation
articles.title: INDIA bloc rally today: What to know about the Ramlila Maidan protest
articles.summary: The Indian National Developmental Inclusive Alliance is staging the Chalo Dilli protest march in New Delhi on November first to demand Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's resignation over alleged electoral roll irregularities. Concurrently, the ruling Bharatiya Janata Party organised counter demonstrations. Delhi traffic police implemented strict diversions while thousands of security personnel monitored the demonstrations.
articles.description: Here’s what to know about the INDIA bloc mega rally in New Delhi, demanding the resignation of CEC Gyanesh Kumar.

articles.headline: Marble dump yard in Rajasthan attracts tourists while endangering villagers
articles.title: ‘Like Kashmir’: How a toxic marble dump yard became a tourist spot in India
articles.summary: A 300-acre marble slurry dumping site in Kishangarh has become a popular tourist destination resembling a snow-clad landscape in India's Rajasthan state. However, approximately 5,000 residents living in nearby villages suffer from severe health complications, including respiratory illnesses, skin allergies, and dental issues. According to studies and local testimonies, toxic dust contaminates soil, ruins crops, and pollutes groundwater supplies.
articles.description: Vast 'snow yard' in otherwise arid Rajasthan attracts hundreds of tourists daily, but residents face major health risks.

articles.headline: United Nations demands independent investigation into staffer death in Houthi custody
articles.title: UN demands investigation after staffer’s death in Houthi custody in Yemen
articles.summary: The United Nations has called for an urgent and transparent investigation into the death of Mohammad el-Shami, an employee of the Office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights who died in Houthi detention in Yemen. Detained since June 2024 alongside over 60 other aid workers on unproven espionage allegations, el-Shami is the second UN staff member to die in custody. UN High Commissioner Volker Turk and Secretary-General Antonio Guterres demanded answers and the immediate release of remaining detainees.
articles.description: Mohammad el-Shami had been held since June 2024, when he and many other UN and NGO workers were accused of being spies.

articles.headline: France protests enter third week as police fire tear gas
articles.title: France protests enter third week as police fire tear gas
articles.description: Police used tear gas to disperse protesters as demonstrations entered a third week ahead in France.

articles.headline: Bolivia declares nationwide state of emergency due to El Nino
articles.title: Bolivia declares state of emergency over El Nino weather pattern
articles.summary: Bolivian President Rodrigo Paz signed a decree establishing a nationwide state of emergency to deploy rescue teams against floods and drought. According to government reports, drought affects 78,000 families across six departments and has killed over 75,000 cattle. Globally, scientists predict the climate phenomenon could cause more than 450,000 deaths.
articles.description: Drought is affecting 78,000 families and has led to loss of over 75,000 cattle, as El Nino due to peak in late 2026.

articles.headline: Evacuees from Oleshky reunite with family during ceasefire
articles.title: Ukrainian evacuees from Russian-occupied Oleshky reunite with family
articles.summary: Exhausted residents from the Russian-occupied Ukrainian town of Oleshky crossed into Ukraine during a six-day humanitarian ceasefire mediated by United States First Lady Melania Trump and Pope Leo XIV. Evacuees who faced severe food shortages and starvation reunited with family at the border, while officials delivered medical aid and supplies.
articles.description: Starved and exhausted residents of Oleshky arrive in Ukraine after months of isolation, but some stay behind.

articles.headline: India’s largest dam planned to counter China faces Indigenous revolt
articles.title: India’s largest dam planned to counter China faces Indigenous revolt
articles.description: Indigenous people of Arunachal Pradesh are protesting a mega dam planned to counter China's upstream hydropower project.

articles.headline: The murder of Javits Frimpong, a bullied schoolboy in The Bronx
articles.title: The murder of Javits Frimpong, a bullied schoolboy in The Bronx
articles.description: Thousands of people have held vigils for a 15-year-old Ghanaian boy who was chased down and killed in New York.

articles.headline: Taiwan deploys ships to monitor Chinese Coast Guard patrol
articles.title: Taiwan says China harassing shipping with east coast patrol
articles.summary: Taiwan deployed its own vessels to monitor two Chinese Coast Guard ships conducting a patrol off Taiwan's east coast. The Taiwanese Coast Guard stated that China was harassing shipping and attempting to exert jurisdiction. Additionally, Taiwan reported that China sent another ship close to the Taiwan-controlled Pratas Islands.
articles.description: Taiwan's Coast Guard said China's "attempts to harass ships at sea through radio ‌communications are a clear expansion of power that violate international law, undermine regional peace and stability, and deviate from reality"

articles.headline: Field trainers prepare enumerators for upcoming population enumeration phase of census
articles.title: Census 2027: What are the new questions, and how are enumerators being trained? | Explained
articles.summary: Field trainers are preparing enumerators in Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Goa and Punjab for the second phase of the census beginning on December 1, 2026. Enumerators will ask forty questions, including thirteen new categories covering details such as caste, religion and Aadhaar numbers, requiring approximately twenty to twenty-five minutes per respondent across blocks of up to eight hundred people.
articles.description: As Uttar Pradesh and three other poll-bound States — Uttarakhand, Goa and Punjab — prepare to launch the second phase of Census 2027 on December 1, field trainers are briefing about 34 lakh enumerators on 40 questions that will require longer, more sensitive interviews and digital data entry, including caste, religion, Aadhaar access and parents’ details

articles.headline: Precious metals post consecutive monthly declines amid rising inflation and rate hike fears
articles.title: Gold, silver lose sheen
articles.summary: Gold and silver recorded negative returns for the second straight month in October due to surging crude oil prices, escalating inflation concerns, and potential United States interest rate increases. Comex gold dropped by 7.26 percent to $3,884.9 per ounce, while Comex silver fell steeply by 19.1 percent to $49.13 per ounce by the end of October, according to data published on November 2.
articles.description: Gold and silver have clocked negative returns. Even the outlook for both gold and silver have turned negative. Precious metal prices are likely to drift lower until resistance level is breached

articles.headline: Talarico draws a packed campus rally, but can he win over young voters?
articles.title: Talarico draws a packed campus rally, but can he win over young voters?
articles.description: Al Jazeera’s @EmmaWithrow attended a packed rally for Democrat Senate Candidate James Talarico at Texas A&M.

articles.headline: US judge dismisses Donald Trump defamation lawsuit against media outlet
articles.title: Judge dismisses Trump's lawsuit against Wall Street Journal over Epstein birthday book
articles.summary: A United States judge dismissed President Donald Trump's ten billion dollar lawsuit against The Wall Street Journal and parent company Dow Jones. Judge Darrin Gayles ruled the defamation case violated the First Amendment and lacked proof of actual malice. The suit followed the newspaper's report on a 2003 birthday book letter concerning Jeffrey Epstein, which Trump denied writing.
articles.description: Trump had sued the media outlet after it published a letter to Epstein purportedly written and signed by the president as part of a birthday book.

articles.headline: Polish president holds crisis talks following suspension of top court judge
articles.title: Polish president holds crisis talks in court standoff
articles.summary: Polish President Karol Nawrocki held urgent crisis talks with political leaders after the sudden suspension of Constitutional Tribunal chief judge Bogdan Swieczkowski. Prime Minister Donald Tusk accused nationalist opposition figures of undermining democracy, while the European Commission urged the president to accept new judge nominations to resolve the constitutional standoff.
articles.description: A dispute over the politicisation of Poland's constitutional court is deepening, with no side appearing to back down.

articles.headline: Trump agrees to grant visa for mother of slain Bronx teenager
articles.title: Mamdani says Trump has agreed to grant visa to mother of Ghanian teen killed in Bronx shooting
articles.summary: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani announced that President Donald Trump agreed to immediately grant a visa to the mother of Javits Frimpong, a 15-year-old immigrant from Ghana who was shot dead in the Bronx. The teenager was killed on Thursday morning while walking to school, and the shooting remains under active police investigation.
articles.description: The teenager, Javits Frimpong, was on his way to school in a Bronx neighbourhood shortly before 9.30 a.m. October 29 when he was shot in the abdomen, New York City police said
